# Custom Events and Attributes

## 

Overview

In addition to the [default user data](doc:default-aiqua-parameters) the Appier SDK automatically collects, you can collect **custom user data** on your website and app using the SDK logging methods. Custom user data consists of free-form attributes and events that you can define depending on your business needs.

  * **Custom attributes** are pieces of information that describe a user, such as their name, city of residence, or date of birth.
  * **Custom events** are user actions, such as viewing a product page or purchasing a product. Events can also contain **event parameters** , which are details about the event, such as the product name, image, and price. AIQUA retains event data for 180 days.



For example, when a user adds a product to their cart, you can log the `product_added_to_cart` event using an Appier SDK logging method. Events contain event parameters that describe the details of the event, such as `product_name`, `product_id`, `product_category`, and `product_image_url`.

![](https://files.readme.io/a3f2c0a-Screen_Shot_2020-02-03_at_2.36.29_PM.png)

* * *

## 

Data logging guidelines

### 

Field names for custom data

Names for custom events, event parameters, and attributes must conform to AIQUA's naming standards; otherwise, features such as [Dynamic Content](doc:dynamic-content-for-personalizing-creatives) and [segmentation](doc:segments-create) may not function properly.

  * **Custom field names can only contain lowercase alphabetical letters (`a-z`), numbers (`0-9`), and underscores (`_`)**.
  * **Custom field names must begin with an alphabetical character (`a-z`) or an underscore (`_`).**

![](https://files.readme.io/7cc2245-example_field_names.png)

The following examples are **valid custom field names** because they begin with an alphabetical character (`a-z`) or underscore (`_`) and don't contain special characters other than underscores (`_`):

  * `checkout_completed_1`
  * `product_purchased`
  * `_productprice_10`
  * `purchase_checkout_3`
  * `subscription_cancelled`



The following table contains examples of **invalid custom field** names:

Invalid field name| Reason  
---|---  
`1checkout.completed`| Invalid because it starts with a number and contains a period (`.`).The first letter of the field name must be an alphabetical letter (`a-z`) or an underscore (`_`). The period (`.`) is not an accepted special character.  
`product-purchased%`| Invalid because it contains a dash (`-`) and a percent sign (`%`), which aren't accepted special characters.  
`_product price{10}`| Invalid because it contains a space and curly brackets (`{}`), which aren't accepted special characters.  
`purchase+checkout(3)`| Invalid because it contains parentheses (`()`), which aren't accepted special characters.  
`subscription: cancelled`| Invalid because it contains a space and a colon (`:`), which aren't accepted special characters.  
  
> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> You can use the following regular expression to validate that a custom field name will be accepted by AIQUA without issues: `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`

### 

Event parameter and user attribute values

  * **Supported data types:** Array, string, integer, float, boolean, object.
  * **Arrays and objects cannot be nested** , e.g. arrays nested in objects, objects nested in objects, and arrays nested in arrays are considered invalid.
  * **Dates must be logged as strings with the[proper date or datetime format](doc:passing-dates-and-times-to-aiqua-servers)**.
  * **Avoid unnecessarily setting a parameter or attribute to an empty value (e.g. a blank string) or null.** Doing so may cause unexpected or undesirable behavior during segmentation.
    * Note: Using the `exists` segmentation condition without specifying a value will include users with parameters set to an empty value or null. For example, if you set the segment's include condition to `phoneNo` `exists`, users with an empty value or null for the `phoneNo` profile parameter will be included in the segment.
  * **Whenever you log an attribute or parameter, ensure that the data type matches the data type you used the first time you logged it**. If an attribute or parameter is logged with a data type different from the one it was initialized with, the value won't be saved. Instead, it will be set to `null`.
    * If you encounter any issues, please contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#771204042804020707180503371607071e12055914181a)) for assistance.



### 

Logging events

  * **If a transaction consists of multiple events, log each event separately.** For example, when a user completes a checkout, two types of events should be logged: `checkout_completed` and `product_purchased`.
  * **When logging an event that consists of multiple products, each event should only correspond to a single product.** Each SDK method call should only contain one `product_id`. AIQUA features such as Recommendation 2.0, [dynamic content inside creatives](doc:dynamic-content-for-personalizing-creatives), and purchased product filtering (for recommendations and dynamic content) may not function optimally if a single event is associated with multiple products.
  * **For common event types, follow the[AIQUA Custom Event Reference](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1PG7kg8Ce1uK6bGPqQGKzuJemSfNmBI5gT-ejdONBRBw/edit#gid=0)**. This reference enumerates common custom event types used by AIQUA features and the parameters they require to function properly.



#### 

Event logging example: Checkout completed with multiple products purchased

In this situation, two types of events should be logged:

  1. **`checkout_completed`** : Indicates that the user has successfully completed the checkout process. This can be used as the single conversion or goal event.
  2. **`product_purchased`** : Indicates that a product was purchased. Log `product_purchased` separately for each product, so that each event corresponds to a single `product_id`. For example, if three products were purchased, this event should be logged three times, each with a different `product_id`.



### 

Logging user attributes

  * **For optimal feature performance, follow the requirements for predefined attributes.** When logging one of these attributes, the name must match the name listed below. For details about which attributes are required for each feature, see Feature-specific requirements.
    * `phoneNo`: The user's phone number. The value should only contain digits 0-9, with no special characters or spaces. For example, `"0123456789"` is valid, while `"+123-456-789-012"` is invalid.
    * `email`: The user's email address.
    * `line_uid`: The user's LINE user ID.
    * `user_id`: The user's ID in your database or CRM.
  * **You can log user attributes when events relating to user data occur, such as when a user adds payment information or completes an account registration**. Use these events as triggers to provide AIQUA with new or updated user attribute data.
  * **If your website has an auto-login feature, we recommend periodically logging the`user_id` attribute.** Doing so allows AIQUA to remap the user to their third-party cookie if it expires before their login cookie. For example, you can log the `user_id` profile parameter on the user's first visit of the day.



* * *

## 

Feature-specific requirements

Some AIQUA features require you to collect specific attributes, events, or event parameters. If you're using one of the features listed in the following table, ensure you log the required data:

Feature | Required data | Recommended data type  
---|---|---  
**Email campaigns** |  `email`: The user's email address. Email addresses are not case-sensitive.  |  string   
**SMS/MMS campaigns** |  `phoneNo`: The user's phone number, including the country code.  |  string   
**Kakao campaigns** |  `phoneNo`: The user's phone number, including the country code.  |  string   
**Tracking attribution value** |  Include the "value to sum" parameter to track the total monetary value associated with an event. Applicable to events such as `product_purchased` or `checkout_completed`.  See the Appier SDK docs for details on how to track "value to sum": 

  * [Web SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/logging-event-information-on-the-web-sdk#logging-value-to-sum)
  * [Android SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/logging-user-events-for-the-android-sdk#logging-valuetosum)
  * [iOS SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/logging-events-with-parameters-for-ios-sdk)
  * [React Native SDK](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/event-and-profile-logging-for-react-native)

| number  
**Recommendation 2.0** |  Include the `product_id`parameter when logging [events required by recommendation models](recommendation-models#required-data-for-recommendation-models). | string  
**[Uploading Offline Users](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/reference/bulk-upload-offline-users)** |  Include one of the following attributes for each user:

  * `user_id`: The user's unique ID in your system (e.g. your CRM system).
  * `email`: The user's email address.
  * `phoneNo`: The user's phone number.
  * `line_uid`: The user's LINE user ID.

|  string   
**[Uploading Offline Events](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/reference/offline-event-getting-started)** |  `user_id`: The user's unique ID in your system (e.g. your CRM system).  |  string   
**(AIXON) Cookie sync** |  `dmpid`: The user's Data Management Platform (DMP) ID.  This is an additional field to collect a cookie-level ID. If you're using AIXON, the user's `dmpid` can be used for ID syncing if you have a cookie-level ID that needs to map to the client-side first-party cookie assigned by the SDK.  | string  
  
> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note for Recommendation 2.0
> 
> [Recommendation 2.0](doc:recommendations-v2) requires you to [onboard your product data feed](doc:product-data-feed) with AIQUA. The product ID in the data feed must match the `product_id` event parameter for AIQUA to be able to match the event with the product in the data feed.

* * *

## 

Logging custom events and attributes via Appier SDK

The type of user data you collect may differ based on your industry or marketing goals. Use the [AIQUA Custom Event Reference](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1PG7kg8Ce1uK6bGPqQGKzuJemSfNmBI5gT-ejdONBRBw/edit#gid=0) as a guide when deciding what custom data to collect.

Once you've determined what type of data you want to collect, use the Appier SDK methods to log custom events and attributes:

  * **Web** : [Logging Data on the Web SDK](doc:logging-data-on-the-web-sdk)
  * **Native Android** : [Logging Android User Attributes](doc:logging-user-profiles-for-the-android-sdk) and [Logging Android User Events](doc:logging-user-events-for-the-android-sdk)
  * **Native iOS** : [Logging iOS User Attributes](doc:logging-user-profile-information-for-ios-sdk) and [Logging iOS User Events](doc:logging-events-with-parameters-for-ios-sdk)
  * **React Native** : [Logging User Events and Attributes for React Native](doc:event-and-profile-logging-for-react-native)



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Don't log [default events and attributes](doc:default-aiqua-parameters) using the Appier SDK methods. This data is automatically tracked by Appier SDK.

* * *

## 

Checkpoint: Validating the custom data is logged properly

To validate that events and attributes are being logged properly by the Appier SDK, go to the AIQUA Dashboard, click your account name in the lower-left corner, then select:

  * **Recent Activity** to see logged user events.
  * **Recent Users** to see logged user attributes.



Logged user events and attributes are listed under the tab for each platform (e.g. **Web** , **Android** , **iOS Production**). You won't be able to select a platform if you haven't integrated the Appier SDK for that platform.

![](https://files.readme.io/3b46f34-validate_logging.png)

# Journey Maps (Legacy)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Legacy feature
> 
> The legacy journey maps feature will be deprecated in the future. We recommend using the [latest journey maps](https://docs.enterprise.appier.com/docs/getting-started-with-journey-maps) for a more intuitive journey builder and better cross-channel integration. Contact your customer success manager for more details.

You can design a journey map that takes your users through a series of marketing messages based on their behavior at each step of the journey. Using the drag-and-drop function, journey maps are created in flowchart-like diagrams to help you visualize the process.

![](https://files.readme.io/3b28810-Screen_Shot_2020-03-02_at_10.11.36_AM.png)

## 

Overview

There are five main components to a journey map: **Audience** , **Entry Action** , **Conditions** , **Notifications** , and **Exit**.

![](https://files.readme.io/bad8ac7-Screen_Shot_2021-05-14_at_10.55.32_AM.png)

  * A journey map starts with an **audience**. If an entry action is selected, users from the targeted audience segment need to complete the **entry action** (e.g. user visited website) to proceed to the next step.
  * Users are targeted by different **notifications** based on the **conditions** they meet (e.g. users who viewed product A received a push about product A). You can add as many notifications and conditions as needed.
  * Users exit the journey when they reach an exit on the map or when they fulfill the **exit criteria** (e.g. user fulfilled the marketing goal by making a purchase).

# (Optional) Receiving Key-Value Pairs

In addition to the default AIQUA campaign fields such as the title, message, and icon URL, you can send custom data to your app by including key-value pairs in your iOS push campaigns.

For example, if you're using an in-house analytics tool to measure campaign performance, you can include key-value pairs in your push campaigns to pass any additional parameters required by your analytics tool.

  1. Add key-value pairs in your campaign
  2. Retrieve key-value pairs



* * *

## 

1\. Add key-value pairs in your campaign

On the AIQUA dashboard, navigate to **Campaigns > Message campaigns**, then go to the campaign creation or settings page for the campaign you want to add key-value pairs for.

Under **Creative** > **Template** , enable **Include key-value pairs** , then add the key-value pairs you'd like to include.

* * *

## 

2\. Retrieve key-value pairs

Refer to the instructions for receiving key-value pairs that correspond to the iOS SDK version your app uses:

  * SDK 8.3.0 and later
  * SDK 8.2.3 and earlier



### 

SDK 8.3.0 and later

Key-value pairs can be retrieved when a user clicks on a push notification by conforming to the `APRPushNotificationNotifierDelegate`, then accessing the `keyValuePairs` (`[String: Any]`) property of the `APRPushNotificationClickModel` object.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    class AppDelegate {
        func application(
            _ application: UIApplication,
            didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey : Any]? = nil
        ) -> Bool {
            AppierSDK.setPushNotificationNotifierDelegate(self)
            return true
        }
    }
    
    extension AppDelegate: APRPushNotificationNotifierDelegate {
        func notificationOnClicked(notifier: APRPushNotificationNotifier, _ notification: APRPushNotificationClickModel) {
            let sortedKeys = notification.keyValuePairs.keys.sorted()
            
            for key in sortedKeys {
                print("\(key):\(notification.keyValuePairs[key] ?? ""),")
            }
        }
    }
    
    
    - (BOOL)application:(UIApplication *)application didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:(NSDictionary *)launchOptions {
        // Override point for customization after application launch.
        QGSdk *qgsdk = [QGSdk getSharedInstance];
        [qgsdk onStart:@"APPIER_APP_ID" withAppGroup:@"APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID" setDevProfile:NO];
        [AppierSDK setPushNotificationNotifierDelegate:self];
        return YES;
    }
    
    - (void)notificationOnClickedWithNotifier:(APRPushNotificationNotifier *)notifier :(APRPushNotificationClickModel *)notification {
        [self qgLoggerWithFormat:@"notificationId: %ld", (long)[notification.notificationId longValue]];
        [self qgLoggerWithFormat:@"displayTime: %f", notification.displayTime.timeIntervalSince1970];
        
        NSArray *sortedKeys = [[notification.keyValuePairs allKeys] sortedArrayUsingSelector:@selector(compare:)];
        
        for (NSString *key in sortedKeys) {
            NSLog(@"%@: %@", key, notification.keyValuePairs[key]);
        }
    }

### 

SDK 8.2.3 and earlier

Key-value pairs can be retrieved by parsing the `content.userInfo["qgPayload"]` property in the `UNNotificationRequest` object in the notification delegate callback.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    func didReceive(_ request: UNNotificationRequest, withContentHandler contentHandler: @escaping (UNNotificationContent) -> Void) {
        if let keyValuePairs = request.content.userInfo["qgPayload"] as? [AnyHashable : Any] {
            for (key, value) in keyValuePairs {
                print("\(key):\(value),")
            }
        }
    
        // Existing QGNotificationSdk code ...
        let qgsdk = QGNotificationSdk.sharedInstance(withAppGroup: APP_GROUP)
        qgsdk?.didReceive(request, withContentHandler: { content in
            contentHandler(content)
        })
    }
    
    
    - (void)didReceiveNotificationRequest:(UNNotificationRequest *)request withContentHandler:(void (^)(UNNotificationContent * _Nonnull))contentHandler {
        NSDictionary *keyValuePairs = request.content.userInfo[@"qgPayload"];
        if (keyValuePairs) {
            for (id key in keyValuePairs) {
                id value = keyValuePairs[key];
                NSLog(@"%@: %@,", key, value);
            }
        }
    
        //Existing QGNotificationSdk code ...
        QGNotificationSdk *qgsdk = [QGNotificationSdk sharedInstanceWithAppGroup:APP_GROUP];
        [qgsdk didReceiveNotificationRequest:request withContentHandler:^(UNNotificationContent *content){
            contentHandler(content);
        }];
    }

# Default Events and Attributes

After integrating your website or app with the Appier SDK, the SDK will begin collecting default events and default attributes automatically without requiring any code changes in your website or app.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note: Web views
> 
> If you're using a web view to display web content inside your app, note that the default data (for example, `page_viewed` and `visited`) won't be collected by the Web SDK—only [custom data](doc:custom-user-data) will be tracked.

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Custom data
> 
> If you'd like to collect additional data not listed on this page, you can log custom data. To learn more, see [Custom Events and Attributes](doc:custom-user-data).

* * *

## 

User events

Name| Platform / Channel| Description  
---|---|---  
`actionClicked`| Android Push| Generated when the user clicks on a customized button in the notification.  
`aiq_cg_received`| In-Web   
Android In-App  
iOS In-App| Generated when an in-app pop-up or in-web campaign is triggered for a user assigned to the control group in an[Experiment](doc:campaigns-experiment).  
`aiq_deep_link_redirected`| Android  
iOS| Generated when the app processes a deep link through the `handleUriOpened()` API. This event captures attribution data from deep links—including the URL, UTM parameters, and timestamps—which can be used for segmentation and analytics. See [Implementing deep links tracking](doc:flutter-deep-links#2-optional-implementing-deep-link-tracking) for details on the parameters tracked.Supported versions: Flutter SDK 3.2.0 or later.  
`aiq_journey_map_exit`| Android  
iOS  
Web| Generated when the user is exited out of the journey map campaign. See how to segment audience using the [Event Parameters](doc:segments-create-conditions#event-parameters) of this event.This event is only generated in journey maps created after August 2021.  
`aiq_notification_blocked`| Android Push| Generated when a notification is blocked due to a delivery restriction (blackout window or time to live).  
`aiq_web_personalization_impression`| Web| Generated when personalized content is loaded on the visited webpage.  
`app_launched`| Android  
iOS| Generated every time the user launches or opens the app.  
`app_uninstalled`| Android  
iOS| Indicates that the user is marked as an uninstall and is only available for mobile apps. It can be used as a segmentation condition for targeting users marked as an uninstall.This is a virtual event that cannot be used as a trigger condition in in-web campaigns, in-app campaigns and customer journey maps.  
`first_app_launched`| Android  
iOS| Generated when the user launches or opens the app for the first time. Supported versions: Android SDK 5.9.2 and above, iOS SDK 5.2.1 and above.This event can be used as a trigger condition in in-app campaigns starting from Android SDK 7.1.0 and iOS SDK 7.11.0. This event cannot be used as a trigger condition in Journey Maps.  
`first_visited`| Android  
iOS  
Web| You can use this parameter to create a segment for users who recently visited the site or app for the first time (e.g. users first visited site in the past 1 day)This is a virtual event generated from timestamps of the user's activities on the website or app. This event cannot be used as a trigger condition in in-web campaigns, in-app campaigns and customer journey maps.  
`notification_browsed`| Android Push  
iOS Push  
| Generated when the user scrolls an item in the slider or carousel push or clicks the ▶▶ button.  
`notification_clicked`| Android Push  
iOS Push  
Web Push  
Email  
LINE  
SMS  
Kakao| 

  * **Push** : Generated when the user clicks on a push notification.
  * **Email** : Generated when the user clicks on a link in an email campaign.
  * **LINE** : Generated when the user clicks on a LINE campaign (carousel or rich message) that redirects to an Appier SDK-integrated app or website. Supported app SDK versions: Android SDK 7.12.0 or later, iOS SDK 7.20.0 or later.
  * **SMS** and **Kakao** : Generated when a user clicks on an AIQUA short URL ([SMS](doc:creatives-sms-mms#track-clicks-with-an-aiqua-short-url), [Kakao](doc:tracking-clicks-for-kakao-campaigns)).

  
`notification_delivered`| Email LINE SMS Kakao| 

  * **Email / SMS / Kakao** : Generated when the Email / SMS / Kakao vendor reports that the notification has been delivered to the user.
  * **LINE** : LINE does not provide delivery data. This event is generated when a LINE notification is sent to the user (same as `notification_sent`). This event will be deprecated in the future.

  
`notification_displayed`| Android Push  
iOS Push| Generated when the push notification is displayed.A notification may be received but not displayed due to errors that result in display failure (e.g. failure to download notification data). Notifications blocked due to delivery restrictions generate an `aiq_notification_blocked` event instead.For iOS, this event will not be generated if rich push notifications are not properly integrated.  
`notification_received`| Android Push  
iOS Push  
Web Push| 

  * **App Push** : Generated when the app push arrives at the end user's device.
  * **Web Push** : Generated when the web push is delivered and shown on the screen.

  
`notification_sent`| Android Push  
iOS Push  
Web Push  
Email  
LINE  
SMS  
Kakao| Generated when a push / email / LINE / SMS / Kakao notification is sent to the user.  
`page_viewed`| Web| The user visits a web page. You can segment audience based on the URL of the webpage.If your website is a single page application (SPA), the SDK doesn't collect `page_viewed` by default. Instead you'll need to [log the event manually](doc:logging-event-information-on-the-web-sdk#logging-page_viewed-for-single-page-applications-spa).  
`qg_carousel_clicked`| Android Push  
iOS Push| Generated when the user clicks on an expanded carousel or slider item.  
`qg_carousel_dismissed`| iOS Push| Generated when the user closes a carousel or slider notification.  
`qg_email_deferred`| Email| The email sent by AIQUA temporarily cannot be delivered, but AIQUA will continue to attempt delivery for 72 hours.  
`qg_email_hard_bounced`| Email| The email sent by AIQUA hard-bounced. This means that the delivery failed due to a permanent reason. For example, the email address does not exist.  
`qg_email_opened`| Email| The email sent by AIQUA was opened.  
`qg_email_processed`| Email| AIQUA receives the email content and prepares to deliver the email.  
`qg_email_resubed`| Email| The user resubscribes to email campaigns.  
`qg_email_soft_bounced`| Email| The email sent by AIQUA soft-bounced. This means that the delivery failed due to a temporary reason. For example, the user's mailbox was full.  
`qg_email_spammed`| Email| The email sent by AIQUA was reported as spam.  
`qg_email_unsubed`| Email| The user unsubscribes from email campaigns.  
`qg_exception`| Android Push| Indicates a system exception for an SDK.  
`qg_inapp_clicked`| Android In-app  
iOS In-app| Generated when the user clicks on an in-app pop-up notification with a valid link, or when the user submits a form in creatives generated with Creative Studio.  
`qg_inapp_closed`| Android In-app  
iOS In-app| Generated when the in-app pop-up notification is closed.  
`qg_inapp_displayed`| Android In-app  
iOS In-app| Generated when an in-app pop-up notification is displayed.  
`qg_inapp_lead_gen`| Android In-app  
iOS In-app| Only supported for creatives generated with Creative Studio. Generated when the user submits a form by clicking on a creative element where the element's "Action" is set to **Submit form**.  
`qg_inapp_received`| Android In-app| Generated when an in-app pop-up notification is fetched from the server.  
`qg_inapp_toggled`| Android In-app  
iOS In-app| Generated when the user clicks on the floating icon of an in-app pop-up campaign or closes the creative.Not supported for creatives generated with Creative Studio.  
`qg_inweb_clicked`| In-web| Generated when the user clicks on the In-Web creative.  
`qg_inweb_closed`| In-web| Generated when the user closes the in-web creative.  
`qg_inweb_displayed`| In-web| Generated when the In-Web creative pops up.  
`qg_inweb_lead_gen`| In-web| Generated when the user submits lead generation form.  
`qg_line_click`| LINE| Generated when the user clicks on a LINE campaign (carousel or rich message) that redirects to an Appier SDK-integrated app or website.Supported app SDK versions: Android SDK 7.12.0 or later, iOS SDK 7.20.0 or later.This event is the same as the `notification_clicked` event for LINE campaigns.  
`qg_rich_push_opened`| iOS Push| Generated when the user expands the carousel and slider notification using the View button or 3D touch.  
`recommendation_clicked`| Web| Generated when a user clicks on a recommended product within the attribution window.This event includes the following parameters which can be used for audience segmentation: `scenario_id`, `model_id`, `recommendation_id`, and `product_id`.Must be logged manually in the iOS, Android, and React Native SDK.  
`recommendation_impression`| Android  
iOS  
Web| Generated when the recommended products of a recommendation scenario are shown to the user.This event includes the following parameters which can be used for audience segmentation: `scenario_id`, `model_id`, and `recommendation_id`.Supported versions: Android SDK 6.5.0 or later, iOS SDK 7.4.0 or later, React Native SDK 1.5.0.To track impressions for REST-API enabled scenarios, this event must be logged manually when using the iOS, Android, or React Native SDK methods.  
`subscribed_to_webpush`| Web Push| The user allows the web push.  
`unsubscribed_to_webpush`| Web Push| The user blocks the web push.  
`visited`| Web| The user visits the website. This event is only generated once a day upon the user's first visit on that day.  
  
* * *

## 

User attributes

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> The Appier SDK doesn't track `qgCountry`, `qgState`, and `qgCity` by default.
> 
> To use these user attributes in segmentation, the value needs to be logged using the pre-defined methods via the Appier mobile SDK. See the pre-defined methods in [iOS SDK](doc:logging-user-profile-information-for-ios-sdk#using-built-in-methods), [Android SDK](doc:logging-user-profiles-for-the-android-sdk#using-built-in-methods), [React Native SDK](doc:event-and-profile-logging-for-react-native#logging-user-attributes), and [Flutter SDK](doc:event-and-profile-logging-for-flutter#logging-custom-attributes).

Name| Platform / Channel| Description  
---|---|---  
`advertiserId`| Android| Identifier for Advertisers (AAID) for Android. To disable automatic AAID collection, see[Android User Data Permissions](doc:android-user-data-permissions).  
`aiq_push_enabled`| Android iOS| A `true` value indicates that app push notifications were allowed by the user.This attribute can be used as a segmentation condition to target users who are not subscribed to app push. You can reach them using other channels such as email or in-app campaigns.This status is updated only when the user opens the app.Supported versions: Android SDK 5.5.3 and above, iOS SDK 4.4.2 and above  
`browser`| Web| The browser used by the user.  
`deviceBrand`| Android iOS| The brand of the user's mobile device.  
`deviceModel`| Android iOS| The model of the user's mobile device. (e.g. Pixel 5, iPhone 8)  
`deviceType`| Web| The type of device used by the user. This parameter can be used to segment audience based on device type. The value can be `mobile`, `tablet` or `desktop`.  
`email_hard_bounced`| Email| A `true` value indicates that the user's email address has hard bounced. These email addresses will be skipped by the system when sending email campaigns.  
`email_unsubscribe`| Email| A `true` value indicates that the users have unsubscribed their email. These email addresses will be skipped by the system when sending email campaigns.  
`gcmId`| Android iOS Web| The FCM token in Android and Web, or the APNS device token in iOS.  
`identified` (Deprecated)| Web| This attribute has been deprecated.  
`IDFA`| iOS| The Identifier for Advertisers (IDFA) for iOS. To enable or disable IDFA collection, see[iOS User Data Permissions](doc:ios-user-data-permissions).  
`IDFV`| iOS| The Identifier for Vendors (iOS).  
`line_channel_id`| LINE| The channel ID of the LINE channel.  
`line_channel_name`| LINE| The channel name of the LINE channel.  
`line_current_follower`| LINE| A `true` value indicates that the user is detected as a follower of the LINE channel.AIQUA detects for new LINE followers once a day.  
`line_first_sync_time`| LINE| The date when the user is detected as a follower of the LINE channel. AIQUA detects for new LINE followers once a day. The detected date may be one day later than users' actual followed date.Contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#fd988e8ea28e888d8d928f89bd9c8d8d94988fd39e9290) to enable segmentation using this parameter.  
`line_uid`| LINE| The LINE UID of users who followed the LINE channel.  
`line_unfollow_time`| LINE| The date when the user is detected as no longer following the LINE channel. AIQUA detects for LINE followers once a day. The detected date may be one day later than users' actual unfollowed date.Contact Appier Support ([[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#8ce9ffffd3fff9fcfce3fef8ccedfcfce5e9fea2efe3e1) to enable segmentation using this parameter.  
`os`| Android iOS Web| The operating system used.  
`permission`| Web| The user's web push subscription status which can be `granted`, `denied`, or `default`.This attribute can be used as a segmentation condition to target users who are not subscribed to web push (e.g. `permission` `is any of` `denied` or `default`). You can reach them using other channels such as email or in-web campaigns.  
`qg_auid`| Web| The identifier for the Appier Enterprise Service Web SDK. You may see this identifier in segments exported from AIXON RFM Insights and AIXON robots.  
`reason`| iOS| This attribute is present with the value `badDeviceToken` when the user's Apple Push Notification service (APNs) token is invalid.See the [iOS troubleshooting page](doc:ios-troubleshooting-faqs#where-does-the-user-attribute-reason-baddevicetoken-come-from) for details.  
`sdkVersion`| Android iOS| The Appier SDK version being used.  
`uninstallTime`| Android iOS Web| The time when the user is detected as no longer subscribed to push (e.g. user blocked push or the push notification failed to sent).  
`userId`| Android iOS Web| The unique user ID AIQUA assigns to the user.• For Web, this is based on third-party cookie.  
• For Android and iOS, a different `userId` is generated for each device and each app.  
`wUserId`| Web| The website user ID (first-party cookie).

# Designing Creatives

Creative Studio provides a powerful interface for designing engaging creatives. Follow the instructions below to learn how to use various elements, manage views, and optimize your designs for different devices with Creative Studio:

  1. Name your template
  2. Add elements
  3. Customize the elements
  4. Preview creatives across devices
  5. Manage creatives with views
  6. Modify animations and manage elements
  7. Save the template



In addition, refer to the best practices to optimize your designs and ensure effective use of Creative Studio's features.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> You can also start with our [prebuilt templates](doc:prebuilt-templates) and customize them for your specific use case to save your time while still achieving a personalized design.

* * *

## 

1\. Name your template

Enter a unique and descriptive name for your template at the top of the interface to quickly identify and manage your work in Creative Studio.

![](https://files.readme.io/947880ad3f9edf6665f7f76b732c5e803af0ae1734d0e04333ef45bc6a1be668-1._naming.png)

* * *

## 

2\. Add elements

The left toolbar offers various types of elements to facilitate interactions with your end users. Drag and drop elements to the creative canvas to add and customize your creatives.

![](https://files.readme.io/1226cc243b8fc16eb34bf3b92eb1330d3309c52962765fe98a525802bac21878-2._elements.png)

  * **[Button](doc:creative-elements#button)** : Add clickable buttons that trigger actions in your creative.
  * **[Checkbox](doc:creative-elements#checkbox)** : Use checkboxes to select multiple options or indicate true/false choices.
  * **[Input field](doc:creative-elements#input-field)** : Allow users to input text or other types of data.
  * **[Radio](doc:creative-elements#radio)** : Use radio buttons to let users select a single option from a list.
  * **[Drop-down list](doc:creative-elements#drop-down-list)** : Allow users to select from a predefined set of options.
  * **[Text element](doc:creative-elements#text-element)** : Display written content to inform or guide users within your creative.
  * **[Image](doc:creative-elements#image)** : Add static images to enhance visuals in your creative.
  * **[Video](doc:creative-elements#video)** : Embed video content to engage your audience within your creative.
  * **[Custom content](doc:creative-elements#custom-content)** : Embed external content or custom code for flexible or unique additions.
  * **[Wheel of fortune](doc:creative-elements#wheel-of-fortune)** : Create interactive spinning elements for gamified experiences.

![Element Selection](https://files.readme.io/d4d570737754583b0c0d6a3e695ecc4268344291b2810b117ce2dd54e4a540da-image.png)

* * *

## 

3\. Customize the elements

Use the right sidebar's four tabs to customize elements within each view:

  * **Settings** : Change element names, adjust accessibility features, define placements, and set animations. Available options may vary depending on the selected element.
  * **Styles** : Customize the appearance of elements by adjusting text styles, background colors, borders, and more. Available options may vary depending on the selected element.
  * **Actions** : Define what happens when users interact with an element (for example, button clicks). Use the **Check** and **Action** sections to define conditions and their corresponding actions. To avoid unexpected behavior, avoid adding actions after the **Exit** action.



> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> See [Creative Elements](doc:creative-elements) to learn more about the customizable options for each element.

![](https://files.readme.io/08ffba4fe0a95393d0989dc07b179d33835795066b8fc94206d3f32aa4019da4-Customize_elements_-_3_tabs.png)

* * *

## 

4\. Preview creatives across devices

Preview how your creative will look on different devices. The central preview area shows how your creative will appear on desktop, mobile, and other devices, ensuring a consistent user experience across all platforms.

![](https://files.readme.io/971b971d009c88d5a43831b807090ec0364636b8f88df6bc2311b386fa7c9934-mobile_friendly.png)

For in-web campaigns, preview your creatives directly on your website by entering the URL and clicking **Preview**.

![](https://files.readme.io/4432864f2d8f965379685a8a4a5cf83e350811b6788855c7bfaf5b9e9fbe698a-6._preview.png)

* * *

## 

5\. Manage creatives with views

In Creative Studio, a creative can consist of multiple views, allowing you to build interactive and multistep web content for your users.

![](https://files.readme.io/eba8415f841d726012216d0294f41c4395d0a86cea1bb9392dde2231231b4ac8-5._manage_views.png)

To manage creatives with multiple views, use the view management panel at the bottom of the interface. **View 1** is added by default. To add more views, click the **+** icon in the rightmost thumbnail and repeat the [add elements](doc:designing-creatives#2-add-elements) step to create additional views.

Switch between views to edit different parts of your creative. Each view represents a step, and all steps are shown as miniature previews in the panel.

![](https://files.readme.io/94ff0e6c4cf71c9d17db86d9dd24c19489a2cba80a8011be105d7b23ef4b080b-5._add_view.png)

* * *

## 

6\. Modify animations and manage elements

The right sidebar provides two key areas for enhancing your creative's functionality and organization:

  * Animation: Control how views transition and animate.
  * Elements: Organize and manage elements within each view.



#### 

Animation

This tab lets you control how views appear and disappear. You can enable animation effects, select the style, and set the duration.

  * **Entrance animation** : Apply effects when the first view appears.
  * **Between views** : Add animation effects for transitions between steps.
  * **Exit animation** : Set the effect when a view closes.

![](https://files.readme.io/76ecde9420118b52169e3302fbb2d9fb84e97297ad7a84a772cd5101457cefd9-Animation.png)

#### 

Elements

In the **Elements** tab, you can manage and reorder elements within a view. The structured tree format helps you navigate through elements, adjust their order, and toggle their visibility.

![](https://files.readme.io/42bb014ad176e1f4adaa8410194300e0b582bb521e42c96d0725fb938f8aa5e8-Sidebar.png)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> If any settings are incomplete, an alert icon will appear. Click the icon to go directly to the incomplete settings.  
>  ![](https://files.readme.io/8c5f80335b33e5dc7b15f4e7f1d2b6e8ab5ac25f7d88b49af3bcc1117f1e2eb3-incomplete_icon.png)

* * *

## 

7\. Save the template

Once you're satisfied with your design, click **Save**.

  * If you're creating a new template, you'll be redirected to the Creative Studio template list.
  * If you're designing from the in-web or in-app campaign creation interface, you'll be redirected back to the campaign creation screen.



#### 

In-web campaigns

To preview your creative on your website, click **Generate link** to create a preview campaign.

![](https://files.readme.io/f27a1e160fb0b47c834116b8d56b81d65a82372973667c08ec9e4b18e0b1d3da-CS-generate-link.png)

#### 

In-app campaigns

Preview in-app creatives directly in the AIQUA dashboard to see how they will display in your app.

![In-App Preview](https://files.readme.io/0f2efda2a8be9d441e783b7f565b503d99cd6b2e7d40dfcb0c94d033859e57d9-CS-in-app-preview.png)

* * *

## 

Best practices

Use these best practices to ensure a smooth user experience across all campaigns:

  * Design and user experience
  * Form handling
  * Interactive elements



### 

Design and user experience

Follow these best practices to design effective campaigns and enhance the user experience:

  * Include a close button
  * Optimize image sizes
  * Ensure mobile responsiveness
  * Highlight required input fields



#### 

Include a close button

For in-app campaigns, always add a close button to allow users to exit the campaign.

![](https://files.readme.io/c112546888ce6ddb555e1eca50fe9b6010f40102b86b0160b73965e5a7c58218-Close_button.png)

#### 

Optimize image sizes

Use smaller images to improve load times and enhance user experience.

#### 

Ensure mobile responsiveness

Consider mobile users when designing your creatives to provide a seamless experience across all devices.

  * Use mobile-optimized templates: Creative templates with **(Mobile)** in the template names are pre-adjusted to fit mobile devices.

![](https://files.readme.io/73156bb073a483c35573e954294f0e33374b7ca236aa011cd038ae9092c20f90-image.png)

  * Modify other templates to make them mobile-friendly:
    1. Use the mobile icon to preview how the creative looks on mobile devices.
    2. Make necessary adjustments to ensure proper display on smaller screens.

![](https://files.readme.io/5ad7e62ec7311fee0ba77e06603de55600ce71d7892fdee5d5f45d56ad35c71c-mobile-device.png)

#### 

Highlight required input fields

Under the **Settings** tab, check **Input required** to highlight elements when users attempt to proceed without entering input or making a selection.

For example, when a radio button element is set to **Input required** , ensure the "Next" button is set up correctly:

  1. Select the "Next" button and go to the **Actions** tab.
  2. Under **...check if...** , ensure there's a condition set to **View inputs are valid**. If no condition is set yet, select **\+ Check** to add one.
  3. Enable the **Highlight check failures** option.

![](https://files.readme.io/f9d73b2f2aeb23a78fff798ec3d064278c895abc318d702a9d2fbd7d60559b19-Input_required.png)

### 

Form handling

Learn how to manage form submissions and input validation:

  * Preventing duplicate submissions
  * Validating form inputs
  * Capture Appier IDs in form submissions



#### 

Preventing duplicate submissions

To avoid multiple submissions of the same form:

  1. Select the "Submit" button and navigate to the **Actions** tab.
  2. Click **\+ Action** and choose **Submit form**.
  3. Add another action: **Change view** to redirect users to a "Thank You" page.

![](https://files.readme.io/21f68978ab9ffb02c0775d9b9a9b43656645ce43bfab72a362f222694ed69142-prevent_repeated_submission.png)

#### 

Validating form inputs

To ensure all required fields are filled correctly:

  1. For each required field (for example, email input):
     * Set the **Input type** appropriately (for example, **Email field**).
     * Check **Input required** in the **Settings** tab.
  2. For the "Submit" button:
     * In the **Actions** tab, set a **Check** condition to **View inputs are valid**.
     * Set the **Action** to **Submit form**.

![](https://files.readme.io/0661d7ebd0bc2c09aae3011009d1481be0678da1bd370afdd2bde521aa5b55b9-Submit_form.png)

#### 

Capture Appier IDs in form submissions

To automatically capture user’s Appier IDs when users submit forms:

  1. In the editor, select **Edit variables and formulas**. Add a custom data field by entering `UserId` as the field name.

![](https://files.readme.io/149e1dce7228f00945322b1f1a408bc65a760d605c8ec6341173c8492be6f034-lead-form-user-id-variable.png)

  2. Click and expand the **Advanced options** > **Open JavaScript editor**. Then, add this script to retrieve and attach the user ID:



JavaScript
    
    
    appier('getUserId', (userId) => {
        $i.dataFields.UserId = userId;
    });

![](https://files.readme.io/ff224c0d25557e41207af92a0c4738d0646d635a713134d028beb4d5f4eb997d-lead-form-user-id-script.png)

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Supported SDK versions
> 
> For In-app campaigns, `getUserId` requires:
> 
>   * Android SDK 8.7.0 or later
>   * iOS SDK 8.5.0 or later
> 


The `UserId` field will appear in your [exported form data](doc:performance-creative-studio#download-form-data), which helps you identify which user submitted each response.

### 

Interactive elements

Discover how to set up engaging interactive features in your campaigns:

  * Discount banner example
  * Limit the number of spins



#### 

Discount banner example

For a discount banner with a "Shop Now" button:

  * No **Check** conditions are needed.
  * Set the **Action** to **URL** to redirect users to the product page when they select the "Shop Now" button.

![](https://files.readme.io/97db876bbdc11bbe3acb8a4cf87fec080a1cf941b311f92ef3c320d647c86779-Check-Action_setting.png)

#### 

Limit the number of spins

When creating interactive creatives with the **[wheel of fortune](doc:creative-elements#wheel-of-fortune)** , follow these steps to limit the number of spins each user can have:

  1. Select the wheel of fortune element, navigate to the **Settings** tab, and set the **number of spins allowed** to limit how many spins each user can have.
  2. Navigate to the **Actions** tab.
  3. Select **\+ Check** , then choose **Spins count** to verify if the user has reached the spin limit.
  4. Select **\+ Action** , and set the first drop-down to **Change view** to display a message like "You've reached your spin limit. Thank you for playing!"

![](https://files.readme.io/9e23478f16f93022340a8919c9e156d8d1844fce4e0315defa2a8acfb879ee04-number_of_spins_allowed.png)

# Dynamic Content

## 

What is dynamic content?

Dynamic content refers to elements used in creatives that change based on each user's behaviors and attributes. Having content relevant and personalized for individual users is crucial for engaging your users.

A typical example is a message that includes the name and image of the products the user has added to cart.

![](https://files.readme.io/5ba0a8b-Screen_Shot_2021-04-22_at_3.11.59_PM.png)

Dynamic content can be based on:

  * User attributes and events
  * Product recommendations
  * Feed triggers



You can add dynamic content to various creative elements, including text (such as titles, messages), URLs (such as deep links, destination URLs), images (such as notification images, icons).

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> To use dynamic content in Email campaigns, see this section.

### 

Supported campaign types

| Attributes & events| Recommendation| Feed trigger  
---|---|---|---  
Message (Regular)| Push: Yes  
SMS: Yes  
Email: Yes  
LINE: Yes  
Kakao Moment: Yes| Push: Yes  
SMS: Yes  
Email: Yes  
LINE: Yes  
Kakao: No| No  
Message (Trigger)| Push: Yes  
SMS: Yes  
Email: Yes  
LINE: Yes  
Kakao: No| Push: Yes  
SMS: Yes  
Email: Yes  
LINE: Yes  
Kakao: No| Push: Yes  
SMS: Yes  
Email: Yes  
LINE: Yes  
Kakao: No  
In-web and in-app| No| No| No  
Journey maps| Push: Yes  
SMS: Yes  
Email: Yes  
LINE: Yes  
In-web: No  
In-app: No| Push: Yes  
SMS: Yes  
Email: Yes  
LINE: No  
In-web: No  
In-app: No| No  
  
> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Notes and limitations
> 
>   * Kakao Moment: Unlike other channels, Kakao requires you to map dynamic content to a specific Kakao variable type to avoid account penalties. For details, see [Variable mapping requirements](doc:creatives-kakao-moment#variable-mapping-requirement).
>   * Recommendation: When using Recommendation as dynamic content in a message regular campaigns, note the following delivery rate:
>     * Push and SMS: AIQUA can deliver up to 50 notifications per second.
>     * Email and LINE: AIQUA can deliver up to 10 - 15 notifications per second.
> 


* * *

## 

Based on attributes and events

You can personalize content using user attributes and events collected via the SDK.

When creating a message campaign, click the `{...}` icon in any field that supports dynamic content, then select **User attributes** or **User events** and add the **Fallback text**. If there is no data for the variable you selected, this text will be displayed. For example, if the notification title contains the user's first name, you can specify a default value to address users who do not have first name data.

![](https://files.readme.io/41b3e350940ab89cbdb5d5c766afcdda7afa437247c6d64394e917a6160ff1d2-dynamic-content-attributes-events.png)

#### 

Common use cases

Goal| Method  
---|---  
Personalize titles| Select user attributes (like `first_name`) or event properties (like `category_viewed`) from the dynamic content dropdown menu.  
  
For example: "Amy, interested in Brand Z shoes?"  
Dynamic images| Select the image URL from a user's last interaction, such as `product_viewed` or `added_to_card`.  
Dynamic deep links| Select the deep link property associated with a user event, and the user will be directed to the specific destination rather than the home page.  
  
For example: `product_viewed > product_deeplink > of the latest event`  
Carousel cards| Select the specific item index (1st, 2nd, 3rd) from the event history to populate each card.  
  
* * *

## 

Based on product recommendations

To personalize creative content using products from [Recommendation](doc:recommendations-v2), you must first create a scenario where the [placement](doc:creating-scenario-recommendation-20#1-choose-a-name-and-placement) is set to **Dynamic content in creative** and the [status](doc:recommendation-scenarios-manage#monitor-scenario-status) is **Ready** or **Updating**.

Once your scenario is ready, choose a setup method based on your channel:

  * Insert via creative settings: Supported for push and LINE message campaigns
  * Generate via syntax generator: Supported for SMS, email, journey maps



### 

Insert via creative settings

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Supported campaign types
> 
>   * Push message campaigns
>   * LINE message campaigns
> 


For [push](doc:campaigns-message-create-push#2-set-up-creatives) and [LINE](doc:campaigns-message-create-line#2-set-up-creatives) message campaigns, you can insert recommendations directly in the **Creative** step. Click the dynamic content icon `{...}` in any supported field (such as **Title** or **Message**), and configure the following settings:

  1. **Scenario** : Select which recommendation scenario to use.
  2. **Display item** : Select the ranking of the product to display. For example, if you select **1st recommended item** , the creative displays the top-ranked (most relevant) match generated by the scenario.
  3. **Product field** : Select which product field to show, for example, product ID, product name, or other product attributes.
  4. **Default text** : Set a default value to display if recommendation data is unavailable.

![](https://files.readme.io/03ae1e4ac9294a1ceb7ae0d1e3fb72c0ff3da20aef7cd090a7b439ce3a93e622-dynamic-content-recommendation-syntax.png)

You can modify these settings at any time to update your dynamic content configuration.

### 

Generate via syntax generator

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Supported campaign types
> 
>   * Message campaigns sent via email and SMS.
>   * Journey maps campaigns sent via app push, web push, email, and SMS.
> 


For channels that don't support the built-in menu, generate the syntax using the [dynamic syntax generator](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/18QMW_a4nu7zbGfkaYCAKCXRbRj30DUNYOD5sncceYYE/edit?usp=sharing):

  1. Make a copy of the spreadsheet, enter your [**App ID** and **API Token**](doc:user-settings), and then click **Update Sheet Setting** to retrieve your available scenarios.
     * Note that Google Sheets will request permission the first time you run the script. You must grant access for the tool to load your data.
  2. Scenario: Select which recommendation scenario to use.
  3. (Optional) Category filter: To restrict recommendations, select the category tab and enter the specific category names.
     * Separate levels with ">", for example, "Clothes > Shirts".
     * Enter exact, case-sensitive category names in the category tab that match your product feed.
  4. Product parameter: Select which product parameter to show, for example, product ID, product name, or other product attributes.
  5. Index number: Select the index that corresponds to the product ranking. For example, enter "0" to indicate the first recommended item, and "1" for second recommended item generated by the scenario.
  6. Default text: Select the checkbox to specify the default value if recommendation data is unavailable. Leave the box unchecked if you've already set a default value in your campaign dashboard.
  7. Once configured, click **Show the Syntax**. Copy the generated code and paste it into the creative element in your campaign dashboard.

![](https://files.readme.io/3c942e370992bdd90c78e321f103dfc0f64101c9ba188f4cc006b99c730918cb-syntax-generator-flow.png)

* * *

## 

Based on feed triggers

Dynamic content can be based on triggers by feed changes. For example, you have set up a trigger campaign that will be sent when there is a 10% price drop in the products added to cart by the user. In the creative of this trigger campaign, you can dynamically show the product added to cart by the user that had a 10% price drop.

To use dynamic content based on feed trigger, add: `{{feed_trigger.event.index.parameter_name}}`

For example, to use a feed trigger based on a product added to cart, add `{{feed_trigger.product_added_to_cart.0.product_name}}`.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Fallback text is not supported in dynamic content based on feed trigger.

* * *

## 

Using product information from your data feed

For dynamic content based on user events or feed trigger, you can also use product information from the data feed for the parameter you want to display. This is useful if the product information you would like to display for dynamic content is in a data feed but not collected by Appier SDK.

  * To use product information from a data feed with user events, add: `{{event.index.feed.parameter_name|default('default_value')}}`
  * To use product information from a data feed with a feed trigger, add: `{{feed_trigger.event.index.feed.parameter_name}}`



> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important
> 
>   * The `parameter_name` must match the column name or field name in the product datafeed. Make sure you don't change the fields of the datafeed after you provide the datafeed to Appier.
>   * When using product information from data feed with user events, the user event must include a `product_id` parameter. AIQUA uses this `product_id` to map the product logged in the event with the product in the data feed.
> 


#### 

Example 1: Using data feed + user event

In the example below:

  * The `product_viewed` is an event collected via SDK.
  * The index 0 indicates the latest `product_viewed` event the user completed.
  * The `retail_price` is a field in the product data feed, but not collected by SDK. The `product_viewed` and `retailed_price` are linked by the same product ID. The retail price of the product last viewed by the user will be shown in the message.



#### 

Example 2: Using data feed + feed trigger

In the example below:

  * The `retail_price` is a field in the product data feed.
  * The message shows the retail price of the product last viewed by the user that has a feed trigger.



* * *

## 

Dynamic content in email campaigns

For email campaigns, you can use dynamic content in the following places.

  * Email subject
  * Drag & drop editor: Text
  * Drag & drop editor: Image
  * Drag & drop editor: Link
  * Drag & drop editor: HTML block
  * HTML editor



* * *

### 

Email subject

To add dynamic content in your email subject:

  1. Click the `{...}` to select either a **User attribute** or a **User event**.
  2. (Optional) Add **Fallback text** to show the text in case there is no data for the variable you selected.

![](https://files.readme.io/bec9121abd1df4aceccf1cccabd71d97a58faa8197775f91788fd14d79310010-email-subject-dynamic-content.png)

* * *

### 

Drag & drop editor: Text

To add a dynamic text:

  1. Inside drag & drop editor, click on a text box to call out the text menu.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> To add a dynamic text based on [Recommendation 2.0](doc:dynamic-content-for-personalizing-creatives#based-on-recommendation-20) or [feed trigger](dynamic-content-for-personalizing-creatives#based-on-feed-trigger), paste the dynamic syntax in the text box.
> 
> To add a dynamic text based on attributes or events, proceed to step 2.

  2. Click **Insert dynamic content**.

![](https://files.readme.io/2068876-Screen_Shot_2022-02-24_at_6.11.29_PM.png)

  3. Select a user attribute or user event from the **Value** drop-down menu.
  4. Type the default value in case the dynamic parameter is not available for some users. The **Default value** is optional, but it's highly recommended to have a fallback.
  5. When you're done setting up your dynamic text, click **Confirm**.

![](https://files.readme.io/2d2083e266bddc4a4fcdaf1aad5f138b9aa41dc62d1434c763e24eeb7945d7ab-email-editor-text.png)

* * *

### 

Drag & drop editor: Image

To add a dynamic image:

  1. Inside drag & drop editor, click on an Image box to access the **Content properties** on the right.
  2. Click the switch next to **Dynamic Image** to enable it and type the dynamic syntax inside **Dynamic URL**. For example: `{{product_added_to_wishlist.0.product_image_url|default("https://www.example.com/jacket.png"}}`

![](https://files.readme.io/3f669a6-Screen_Shot_2020-06-29_at_6.26.08_PM.png)

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important
> 
> The link inside the **URL** field below the **Dynamic URL** is not the fallback image if there is no dynamic content matched with the user. It is the URL link for adding static image.

![](https://files.readme.io/15ab86a-b1fa895-regular_campaign_design_email_content_image_dynamic_dynamic_image_url_field_marked.png)

* * *

### 

Drag & drop editor: Link

You can add a dynamic link to text, videos, and buttons.

To add a dynamic link:

  1. Inside the drag & drop editor, go to the URL field.
     * **Text URL** : Click on a text box to call out the text menu, click the **Insert link** icon to find the **Url** field.

![](https://files.readme.io/a32edcd-Screen_Shot_2022-02-24_at_7.32.39_PM.png)

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> You can also add dynamic syntax to the **Text to display** field if needed.

  * **Video URL** : Click on a video and find the **Video url** field in the **Content properties** on the right.

![](https://files.readme.io/7023527-Screen_Shot_2022-02-24_at_6.37.41_PM.png)

  * **Button URL** : Click on a button and find the **Url** field in the Content Properties on the right.

![](https://files.readme.io/a0c616a-Screen_Shot_2022-02-24_at_6.42.51_PM.png)

  2. In the **Url** or **Video url** field, type the dynamic syntax. For example: `{{product_viewed.0.product_url|default("https://www.example.com/jacket02/")}}`

# Email Templates

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Email templates are only supported in regular campaigns and trigger campaigns. This feature is **not** supported in email campaigns inside the legacy journey maps.

## 

Creating email templates

  1. To create an email template, click **My templates** , and select **Email templates**.

![](https://files.readme.io/bc59c02-Screen_Shot_2022-10-17_at_10.49.10_AM.png)

  2. Click **\+ Create new template**.

![](https://files.readme.io/4f9e0bd-Screen_Shot_2022-10-17_at_10.50.16_AM.png)

  3. Select one of the three methods to create an email template.
     * **Default templates** : Modify from a default template provided by Appier.
     * **My templates** : Modify from an existing template you have previously created.
     * **Create your own** : Create a template from scratch.

![](https://files.readme.io/c6997b2-Screen_Shot_2022-10-17_at_10.52.36_AM.png)

  4. Design your email template. For more details on how to use the email editors, see [**drag & drop editor**](doc:design-email) or [**HTML editor**](doc:email-html-editor).
  5. When you are done, click **Save** and name the template. If you add a tag, you will be able to search for templates by tags.

![](https://files.readme.io/993afff-Screen_Shot_2022-10-17_at_10.54.34_AM.png)

* * *

## 

Managing email templates

In the email template list, you can use the following functions to find your template.

  * **Search template** : Search by the template name.
  * **Type** : Select **Drag & Drop Editor** or **HTML Editor** to filter based on the email editor used to create the template.
  * **Tag** : Filter based on the tags added to the templates.
  * **Sort by** : Select **Last edit** to sort by last edited time or select **Template name** to see the templates in alphabetical order.

![](https://files.readme.io/97f4561-Screen_Shot_2022-10-17_at_10.40.39_AM.png)

You can use the menu icon under each template to edit, duplicate, or delete the template. You can also create a campaign with this template.

![](https://files.readme.io/36d2720-Screen_Shot_2022-10-17_at_10.37.49_AM.png)

* * *

## 

Using templates in email campaigns

You can apply a template to email campaigns either from the email template list or by selecting the template from the Create Campaign page.

  * Option 1: In the email template list, click the menu icon of the template and select **Create regular campaign** or **Create trigger campaign**.

![](https://files.readme.io/bea8890-Screen_Shot_2022-10-17_at_10.35.36_AM.png)

  * Option 2: When creating campaigns, click **\+ Add email creative** on the **Creative** section and select **My templates** to find the template you have created previously.

![](https://files.readme.io/c332f0ebdf882ab5b07b49e0e8c50b66477f92b47b6860b3cee2d84cf0b51366-creative-email-my-template.png)

After you have selected a template, you can make further adjustments if needed and save the modified template to this campaign. If you want to save this modified template as a new template for future use, click **Save as new template**.

![](https://files.readme.io/d451aef863457def32dc0ed3cbf9a9e810455ebb5a7ea8e62a808258f22726ea-save-as-new-template.png)

# Enabling Capabilities

After [installing the iOS SDK](doc:installing-the-appier-ios-sdk-v2), you need to follow the steps to enable the capabilities required for user tracking and the APNS token and enable App Group to initialize the SDK.

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important
> 
> Only do this for the main application target. Do not do this for Service Extension or Content Extension.

  1. Go to **Project > Main Target > Signing & Capabilities**.
  2. Click **\+ Capability** , enable **Background Modes** , and select the following checkboxes:


  * **Background fetch**
  * **Remote notifications**

![](https://files.readme.io/aa43c67-Screen_Shot_2020-06-03_at_6.41.11_PM.png)

  3. Click **\+ Capability** and enable **Push Notifications**.

![](https://files.readme.io/7f7a40d-Screen_Shot_2020-06-03_at_6.00.54_PM.png)

You will see that the following capabilities are enabled.

![](https://files.readme.io/0586573-Screen_Shot_2020-06-03_at_6.45.48_PM.png)

  4. Under the **All** tab, click **\+ Capability** , add an **App Group** and enter the App Group ID (hereby referred to as `APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID`).



> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> What is my APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID (App Group ID)?
> 
> The APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID is "`group.YOUR_BUNDLE_ID.notification`". For example, if your iOS **Bundle Identifier** is "com.appier.docs.SampleProject", your **APPIER_APP_GROUP_ID** is "group.com.appier.docs.SampleProject.notification".

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important:
> 
>   * If you want to change your App Group ID, make sure you are using iOS SDK 7.7.0 or above. In earlier SDK versions, changing the App Group ID will result in iOS users being duplicated.
>   * This App Group ID will later be used when setting up SDK initialization and rich push notifications. Be sure to use the same App Group ID you've entered here.
> 


![](https://files.readme.io/4ba3f35-Screen_Shot_2020-06-05_at_5.16.19_PM.png)

# Registering Your App with AIQUA

## 

Prerequisites

### 

Prepare your Google Play Store URL

Prepare your Google Play Store URL in the proper format. Remove the language setting (the `hl` query parameter) from the URL before entering it on the AIQUA dashboard.

Original URL| Formatted URL  
---|---  
`https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.appier.aiqua.app&hl=tw_zh`| After removing the `hl` query parameter (`&hl=tw_zh`):`https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.appier.aiqua.app`  
  
### 

Using your own key

If you'd like to use your own service account private key or FCM key to register your app instead of AIQUA's default push credentials, follow the instructions below to create the credentials:

  * Service account private key
  * FCM key (Please note that the use of FCM keys will be retired in June 2024, and service account private keys will be required instead.)



> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> AIQUA's default credentials
> 
> If you want to use AIQUA's default push credentials, no additional setup is needed, and you can continue with registering your app on the AIQUA dashboard.

#### 

Using your own service account private key

If you'd like to use your own service account private key rather than using the private key provided by AIQUA, complete the following steps before registering your app on the AIQUA dashboard.

  1. Go to the [Firebase console](https://firebase.google.com/) and select a project or create a new project. [Create a service account](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-accounts-create) if you don't have one already.
  2. Go to the **Project settings** page and click the **Cloud Messaging** tab.

![](https://files.readme.io/4332591-cloud-messaging-settings.png)

  3. If **Firebase Cloud Messaging API (V1)** isn't enabled for your project, enable it by clicking **Manage API in Google Cloud Console** , then clicking **Enable**.

![](https://files.readme.io/a62ce3d-enable-firebase-cloud-messaging-api.png)

  4. Generate your service account private key. From the **Project settings** page, go to the **Service accounts** tab. Click **Generate new private key** , then in the modal that appears, click **Generate key** to begin downloading your private key.



> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Save your private key in a secure location—this key can't be recovered if it's lost.

![](https://files.readme.io/375a817-generate-service-account-private-key.png)

Your private key will be downloaded as a JSON file. Save this file and upload it when registering your app on the AIQUA dashboard.

#### 

Using your own FCM key

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> FCM keys retiring
> 
> Please note that the use of FCM keys will be retired in June 2024, and service account private keys will be required instead.

If you have your own Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) key, have your FCM server key and FCM sender ID ready to upload to the AIQUA Dashboard.

  1. Log in to the [Firebase Console](https://console.firebase.google.com/).
  2. Go to the **Project settings** page and click the **Cloud Messaging** tab.
  3. Enable **Cloud Messaging API (Legacy)**. Click the three-dot vertical menu, click **Manage API in Google Cloud Console** , and on the Google Cloud Console, click **Enable**.

![](https://files.readme.io/5221283-fcm-enable.png)

  4. Once you've enabled the Cloud Messaging API, your FCM server key and sender ID will be visible under **Cloud Messaging API (Legacy)** :

![](https://files.readme.io/14e6609-fcm-key-sender-id.png)

* * *

## 

Registering your app on the AIQUA dashboard

  1. On the AIQUA dashboard, go to **Settings > Integration** and select **Android**.

![](https://files.readme.io/ab270d7c8ba3bf380e733892695f3f40ed972918dea858aa25cb3793a2d0c78c-integration-android.png)

  2. On the Android integration page, enter your app's Google Play Store URL without the language settings (the `hl` query parameter).

![](https://files.readme.io/daad2ad-play-store-url.png)   


  3. Select **I use FCM in my app**. GCM has been deprecated by Google.

![](https://files.readme.io/ed6aa4d-key-type.png)

  4. Under **Key Type** , select one of the following options:
     1. **I will use AIQUA 's FCM Key**: If you'd like to use AIQUA's FCM key, select this option.
     2. **I have my own key** :
        1. If you have your own FCM key, select this option and enter your **FCM Key** and **Sender ID**.
        2. If you have your own service account private key, upload the JSON key by going to **Service Account Private Key** and clicking **Upload key**.



> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> FCM keys retiring
> 
> Please note that the use of FCM keys will be retired in June 2024. If you'd like to continue using your own push credentials, service account private keys will be required instead.

  5. (Optional) To enable heads-up notifications by default for all new campaigns, select **Enable heads-up notifications**.

![](https://files.readme.io/673abfa-enable-hun.png)

  6. Click **Next** to finish registering your app with AIQUA.



After you've finished registering your app, use Android Studio to [install the Appier Android SDK](doc:installing-in-android-studio).

* * *

## 

Heads-up notifications

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Heads-up notifications are only supported for apps using **Android SDK 5.6.1 or later**.

[Heads-up notifications (HUNs)](https://source.android.com/devices/automotive/hmi/notifications/hun) are notifications that briefly appears as a floating window on unlocked Android devices running Android 5.0 (Lollipop) or later.

If you don't want to enable HUNs by default for all campaigns, you can enable them for specific campaigns by going to the campaign's creative settings, and under **Display settings** , checking **Enable heads-up notifications**.

![](https://files.readme.io/57cfddd-android-heads-up-push.png)

# Logging Custom User Data for Flutter

> 👍
> 
> See [Custom Events and Attributes](doc:custom-user-data) for detailed guidelines on defining and logging custom data.

## 

Overview

Custom user data consists of free-form attributes and events that you can define depending on your business needs. Custom data isn't collected by the Appier SDK by default; instead, these custom events and attributes must be manually logged using the SDK logging methods as described below.

* * *

## 

Logging custom attributes

### 

Using built-in methods

The Flutter SDK provides the following built-in methods for logging custom user attributes:

Dart
    
    
    Future<void> setUserId(String userId)
    Future<void> setName(String name)
    Future<void> setFirstName(String firstName)
    Future<void> setLastName(String lastName)
    Future<void> setCity(String city)
    Future<void> setEmail(String email)
    Future<void> setPhoneNumber(String phoneNo)
    Future<void> setDayOfBirth(int day)
    Future<void> setMonthOfBirth(int month)
    Future<void> setYearOfBirth(int year)

#### 

Example: Built-in methods

Use the method corresponding to the attribute you want to log. For example:

  * To log the user's name attribute, call `setName()`
  * To log the user's email attribute, call `setEmail()`
  * To log the user's year of birth attribute, call `setYearOfBirth()`



Dart
    
    
    AppierFlutter.setName('NAME')
    AppierFlutter.setEmail('[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)')
    AppierFlutter.setYearOfBirth(1997)

### 

Using custom keys

In addition to using the built-in methods, you can also specify which type of custom data to log by using `setCustomKey()` and specifying a value for `key`, where `key` is the custom attribute you want to log:

Dart
    
    
    Future<void> setCustomKey(String key, dynamic value)

#### 

Example: Custom keys

In the following example, `setCustomKey()` is used to set the user's current rating:

Dart
    
    
    // Sets the value of the `rating` attribute to 5
    AppierFlutter.setCustomKey('rating', 5);

#### 

Clearing attributes using `setCustomKey()`

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Setting an attribute to `null` may result in [unexpected segmentation behavior](doc:custom-user-data#event-parameter-and-user-attribute-values).

To clear the value of a user attribute with `setCustomKey()`, log a null value.

Dart
    
    
    // Clears the user's `rating` attribute by logging a null value
    AppierFlutter.setCustomKey('rating', null);

* * *

## 

Logging custom events

Events can be tracked with `logEvent()`. `eventName` is the only required parameter; all other parameters are optional.

Dart
    
    
    Future<void> logEvent(String eventName, {Map<String, dynamic>? parameters, double? vts, String? vtsCurr})

Parameter| Type| Description  
---|---|---  
`eventName`| `String`| Required. Event name  
`parameters`| `Map`| Optional. Parameters for the event  
`vts`| `double`| Optional. Monetary value associated to the event  
`vtsCurr`| `String`| Optional. Currency code of the value to sum  
  
### 

`vts` and `vtsCurr`

Include `vts` when logging an event to track the monetary value associated with the event (e.g. the total conversion value associated with a `checkout_completed` event), and log `vtsCurr` to specify an ISO 4217 currency code.

### 

Event logging example

The following example logs a `product_viewed` event and includes metadata such as `name`, `image_url`, and `category`, as well as a `vts` of "100" and a `vtsCurr` of "USD", meaning that the monetary value associated with this event is $100 USD.

Dart
    
    
    AppierFlutter.logEvent(
      "product_viewed",
      parameters: {
        "product_id": "E0238",    
        "product_name": "Brand A Shoes",
        "produdt_image_url": "https://www.example.com",
        "category_name": "Fashion"
      },
      vts: 100,
      vtsCurr: "USD"
    )

* * *

## 

Checkpoint

Follow the steps below to validate that attributes are being logged properly.

  1. Launch your app and complete the action that logs the user attribute.
  2. On the AIQUA dashboard, go to **Settings > Recent Users**.
  3. Under the **Android** tab, you should be able to see the logged user attributes under the **Other fields** column. Note that it can take several minutes for attributes to display on this page.

# Logging Custom User Data for React Native

> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> Before you start, refer to the guidelines for logging [Custom Events and Attributes](doc:custom-user-data).

## 

Logging user events

Event property| Description  
---|---  
`eventName`| Event name  
`parameters`| A dictionary of all the parameters for the event  
`valueToSum`| Monetary value associated to the event  
`currency`| Currency code of the value to sum  
  
JavaScript
    
    
    RNAiqua.logEvent(eventName)
    RNAiqua.logEvent(eventName, parameters)
    RNAiqua.logEvent(eventName, valueToSum)
    RNAiqua.logEvent(eventName, valueToSum, currency)
    RNAiqua.logEvent(eventName, parameters, valueToSum)
    RNAiqua.logEvent(eventName, parameters, valueToSum, currency)

* * *

## 

Logging user attributes

Refer to the following sample values when logging user attributes.

JavaScript
    
    
    RNAiqua.setUserId('USER_ID')
    RNAiqua.setName('NAME')
    RNAiqua.setFirstName('FIRST_NAME')
    RNAiqua.setLastName('LAST_NAME')
    RNAiqua.setCity('CITY')
    RNAiqua.setEmail('[[email protected]](/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection)')
    RNAiqua.setDayOfBirth(1)
    RNAiqua.setMonthOfBirth(7)
    RNAiqua.setYearOfBirth(1997)
    RNAiqua.setPhoneNumber('0912345678') 
    RNAiqua.setCustomKey('KEY_STR', 'strval')
    RNAiqua.setCustomKey('KEY_BOOL', true)

* * *

## 

Checkpoint

Follow the steps below to validate that attributes are being logged properly.

  1. Launch your app and complete the action that logs the user attribute.
  2. On the AIQUA dashboard:
     1. Go to **Settings > Recent Activity** to view logged user events.
     2. Go to **Settings > Recent Users** to view logged user attributes.
  3. Select **Android** , **iOS production** , or **iOS development** depending on the device you're using. Note that it can take several minutes for attributes to display on this page.

# Event Attribution

To track how notifications are affecting the metrics on your app, events attributed to campaign notifications are listed as attributed events in the **Campaign performance** page.

An event can be attributed to a campaign based on:

  * **View-through attribution** : If the event happens within one hour after the user receives a notification, AIQUA attributes it as a view-through.
  * **Click-through attribution** : If the event happens within 24 hours after the user clicks on a notification, AIQUA attributes it as a click-through.



For more details on how event attribution works, see [Understanding Event Attribution](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution).

* * *

## 

Adjusting attribution window

By default, the click-through attribution window (time interval) is set to 86,400 seconds (24 hours) while the view-through attribution window is set to 3,600 seconds (one hour).

You can change this time window using the following APIs. The event attribution window will apply to both iOS app push campaigns and iOS in-app campaigns.

API
    
    
    // to set click through attribution window
    (void)setClickAttributionWindow:(NSInteger)seconds;
    // to set view through attribution window  
    (void)setAttributionWindow:(NSInteger)seconds;

To set a custom attribution window interval, specify a value for `seconds`.  
Below is an example of setting the click-through attribution window to 12 hours (43200 seconds):

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().setClickAttributionWindow(43200)
    
    
    [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] setClickAttributionWindow:43200];

Below is an example of setting the view-through attribution window to two hours (7200 seconds):

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    QGSdk.getSharedInstance().setAttributionWindow(7200)
    
    
    [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] setAttributionWindow:7200];

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Starting from iOS SDK 7.6.0, view-through and click-through attribution window can't be set to zero. If set to zero, the attribution window will fall back to its default value.

# Logging Custom User Data for Android

> 👍
> 
> See [Custom Events and Attributes](doc:custom-user-data) for detailed guidelines on defining and logging custom data.

## 

Overview

**Custom user data** consists of free-form attributes and events that you can define depending on your business needs. Custom data isn't collected by the Appier SDK by default; instead, these custom events and attributes must be manually logged using the SDK logging methods as described in the following pages:

  * [Logging Custom User Attributes for Android](doc:logging-user-profiles-for-the-android-sdk)
  * [Logging Custom User Events for Android](doc:logging-user-events-for-the-android-sdk)



## 

Event attribution

To understand how campaign events are attributed under default settings, and how to adjust the default attribution window, see the [Event Attribution for Android](doc:event-attribution-android-sdk).
