# Logging Custom User Data for iOS

> 👍
> 
> See the [Custom Events and Attributes](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/custom-user-data) for detailed guidelines on defining and logging custom data.

## 

Overview

**Custom user data** consists of free-form attributes and events that you can define depending on your business needs. Custom data isn't collected by the Appier SDK by default; instead, these custom events and attributes must be manually logged using the SDK methods described in the following pages:

  * [Logging Custom User Attributes for iOS](doc:logging-user-profile-information-for-ios-sdk)
  * [Logging Custom User Events for iOS](doc:logging-events-with-parameters-for-ios-sdk)



## 

Event attribution

To understand how campaign events are attributed under default settings and how to adjust the default attribution window, see [Event Attribution for iOS](doc:event-attribution-ios-sdk).

# How do I see conversion value in campaign performance?

Let's say you are tracking `checkout_completed` events on your website or app, and you want to be able to see the conversion value in the campaign performance page and downloaded performance reports.

![](https://files.readme.io/a383f6c-Screen_Shot_2021-05-31_at_3.31.42_PM.png)

To have the monetary value of events tracked under **Conv. Value** :

  * **Requirement 1** : You need to select the events you want to use as conversion events in the [Account Settings](doc:user-settings#conversion-and-attribution) page.
  * **Requirement 2** : The conversion events need to be attributed to the campaign. See [Understanding Event Attribution](doc:performance-and-reports-understanding-event-attribution).
  * **Requirement 3** : You need to include the event's monetary value with `valueToSum` parameter when tracking the events.



The following example demonstrates how to log a `checkout_completed` event with `valueToSum` using the Appier Web SDK, where the purchase value is 4000:

With valueToSum
    
    
    appier("event", "product_purchased", {"product_id": "p123", "product_name": "Brand Z shoes"}, 4000);

If the `valueToSum` parameter is not added, the event will still be tracked, but without a conversion value. You don't need to include `valueToSum` when tracking event that aren't associated with monetary value. The following example shows how you might log such as event:

Without valueToSum
    
    
    appier("event", "product_purchased", {"product_id": "p123", "product_name": "Brand Z shoes"});

For more details on how to track `valueToSum`, refer to the links below:

  * **Web SDK** : [Tracking User Events for Web](doc:logging-event-information-on-the-web-sdk#logging-value-to-sum)
  * **Android SDK** : [Tracking User Events for Android](doc:logging-user-events-for-the-android-sdk#logging-valuetosum)
  * **iOS SDK** : [Tracking User Events for iOS](doc:logging-events-with-parameters-for-ios-sdk)
  * **React Native SDK** : [Tracking Events and Attributes for React Native](doc:event-and-profile-logging-for-react-native)

# Why can't I find some of my past campaigns?

  * Only campaigns that have been updated within the past 180 days are shown on AIQUA dashboard.
  * If it's an archived campaign, make sure the **Show archived campaigns** checkbox is selected.

# Why do some users have different userId and wUserId?

On AIQUA Dashboard, click your account name in the lower-left corner, go to **[Recent Users](https://aiqua.appier.com/recent_users)** and select the **Web** tab. You will see the `userId` listed under the USER ID column and the `wUserId` listed under OTHER FIELDS column.

This FAQ explains why some web users have the same ID for both `userId` and `wUserId`, while other web users have a `userId` that is different from their `wUserId`.

![2234](https://files.readme.io/8107f50-Screen_Shot_2021-01-04_at_10.32.47_AM_copy_2.png)

### 

userId

  * `userId` is the ID for third-party cookie.
  * This is used by AIQUA as the unique ID to identify users.
  * When the user visits a website integrated with Appier Web SDK for the first time, a `userId` is generated.
  * The user will be assigned the same `userId` across websites, meaning that when this user visits other websites integrated with Appier Web SDK, AIQUA will use the same `userId` for this user.



### 

wUserId

  * `wUserId` is the first-party cookie ID.
  * For each Appier SDK-integrated website the user visits, Appier Web SDK generates a new `wUserId`.
  * The user will have a different `wUserId` on each websites.



As a result, if your website is the first Appier SDK-integrated website visited by the user, you may see these users having the same ID for `userId` and `wUserId`. If the users have previously visited other Appier SDK-integrated websites, they will have a `wUserId` that is different from their `userId`.

# Product Filter Rules

Learn how to filter the results returned by your scenario.

Create rules to filter by product attributes, such as category, name, or price. Only products which match your filters will be returned by the scenario.

  * Scenario settings
  * API calls



* * *

## 

Scenario settings

To add product filters, go to the scenario's creation or edit page, then go to **Business rules > Product filter**.

![](https://files.readme.io/c5c51895b339457e852e6f0f71dd2b3395617fed472d3f410308e211740c2759-scenario-product-filter.png)

You can add multiple rules to the filter. Toggle `or`/`and` to specify whether a product needs to meet any or all of the rules to be included in results.

![](https://files.readme.io/0a9a687e696c6371f4ecd7f09cb7ed0ab1ee7480ca834b9049146b49006fa429-product-filter-rule-operator-toggle.gif)

Each rule contains at least one condition for specific attributes, such as the product ID, name, or category.

  * Toggle `or`/`and` to specify whether any or all conditions must be satisfied for this rule to be met.
  * Different comparison operators are available for each data type. For details, see Filter condition operators.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Text values are not case sensitive for filters created from the AIQUA dashboard.

![](https://files.readme.io/c49b21c710ddfea0c244efe961131a05e792a5825680aaa190ab19237a1168d5-product-filter-rule-operator-toggle.gif)

* * *

## 

API calls

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> Filters sent in API calls won't be used unless the **Append API filtering rules** options is enabled in the scenario's settings (**Business rules > Product filter**).
> 
> ![](https://files.readme.io/14e48087dd55d381aaa03496f73577c0185083d659175da0e4c73abc85425020-scenario-product-filter-append-api-rules.png)

You can specify filters for the following product attributes when requesting recommendations via SDK or the [Recommendation API](ref:recommendation-getting-started). Please note the following:

  * Filter values can't contain special characters (`?`, `*`,`+`,`(`, `)` ,`{`,`}`,`[`,`]`,`.` , `^`, `$`, `\` , `|`).
  * Strings are not case sensitive for filters created from the AIQUA dashboard.



Here are some examples of filter objects:

One rule, one conditionOne rule, multiple conditionsMultiple rules, multiple conditions
    
    
    /*
    
    Rule condition: The product category contains they keyword "shoes"
    
    */
    
    {
      "version":2,
      "filterRule":{
          "operator":"OR",
          "ruleList":[
              {
                  "operator":"OR",
                  "conditionList":[
                      {
                          "key":"category",
                          "operator":"in",
                          "value":["shoes"]
                      }
                  ]
              }
          ]
      }
    }
    
    
    /*
    
    * Rule condition: The product has a discounted price less than "500" AND
    * Rule condition: The product category contains the keyword "jeans"
    
    */
    
    {
      "version": 2,
      "filterRule": {
        "operator": "OR",
        "ruleList": [
          {
            "operator": "AND",
            "conditionList": [
              {
                "key": "price",
                "operator": "lt",
                "value": [
                  "500"
                ]
              },
              {
                "key": "category",
                "operator": "contains",
                "value": [
                  "jeans"
                ]
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }
    
    
    /*
    
    * Rule 1:
      * Condition 1: The product belongs to the category "woman's > boots" OR
      * Condition 2: The product category contains the keyword "jeans"
    
      AND
    
    * Rule 2:
      * Condition 1: The value of the custom label equals "true" AND
      * Condition 2: The product title doesn't contain the word "unisex"
    
    */
    
    {
      "version": 2,
      "filterRule": {
        "operator": "AND",
        "ruleList": [
          {
            "operator": "OR",
            "conditionList": [
              {
                "key": "category",
                "operator": "in",
                "value": [
                  "woman's > boots"
                ]
              },
              {
                "key": "category",
                "operator": "contains",
                "value": [
                  "jeans"
                ]
              }
            ]
          },
          {
            "operator": "AND",
            "conditionList": [
              {
                "key": "customLabel01",
                "operator": "eq",
                "value": [
                  "true"
                ]
              },
              {
                "key": "title",
                "operator": "not_contains",
                "value": [
                  "unisex"
                ]
              }
            ]
          }
        ]
      }
    }

Key| Description  
---|---  
`version`| A required parameter. Must be `2`.  
`filterRule`| A complete list of filter rules, consisting of one or more `ruleList` objects and an operator.  
`filterRule.operator`| The operator for this `filterRule` object to be applied to when evaluating `ruleList` objects. Accepted values: `AND`, `OR`.  
`filterRule[].ruleList`| A set of filter rules evaluated with an operator.  
`filterRule[].ruleList[].operator`| An operator for this `ruleList` to be applied to when evaluating `conditionList` objects. Accepted values: `AND`, `OR`.  
`filterRule[].ruleList[].conditionList`| A single rule based on a product attribute.  
`filterRule[].ruleList[].conditionList[].key`| The product attribute being evaluated. Accepted values:

  * `category`
  * `originalPrice`
  * `price`
  * `productId`
  * `title`
  * `customLabel00`,`customLabel01`, `customLabel02`, `customLabel03`,`customLabel04`,`customLabel05`

  
`filterRule[].ruleList[].conditionList[].operator`| The operator to apply to the product attribute. Supported operators differ based on the attribute's data type. See the Filter condition operators for details.  
`filterRule[].ruleList[].conditionList[].value`| The value to evaluate the product attribute against. Not case-sensitive.  
  
* * *

## 

Filter condition operators

The available comparison operators differ based on the data type.

  * String (text values)
  * Float (numerical values)
  * Boolean (true/false values)



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> The operators listed below are valid for filter rules created in scenario settings and API calls. This section does not apply to filter rules set in dynamic content syntax.

### 

String

The following operators are supported for `productId`, `title` (Product Name), and custom labels with the data type set to string.

Operators (AIQUA dashboard)| Operators (API calls)| Description  
---|---|---  
`is any of`| `in`| The data feed value includes at least one of the filtering values.**Example** The data feed value is `Blue Jeans`. If the filter value is: • `Blue Jeans` or `shoes` → Match • `Classic Blue Jeans`→ Not a match • `Jeans` → Not a match  
`is not`| `nin`| The data feed value does not include any of the filtering values.  
`contains`| `contains`| The data feed value contains and partially matches at least one of the filtering values.**Example** The data feed value is `Blue Jeans`. If the filter value is: • `Jeans` or `shoes` → Match • `Classic Blue Jeans` → Not a match  
`does not contain`| `not_contains`| The data feed value doesn't contain any exact matches with the filtering values.  
`starts with`| `starts_with`| The data feed value starts with the filtering value.**Example** The data feed value is `Blue Jeans`. If the filter value is: • `Blue` → Match • `Blu` → Match  
`ends with`| `ends_with`| The data feed value ends with the filtering value.  
  
#### 

String: Product category

The product category is a special field that supports string values with a hierarchical structure, and a product can be a part of multiple categories.

For example, in the nested product category `Women's > Blue Jeans`:

  * `Women's` is the main category.
  * `Blue jeans` is a sub-category.



A product titled `Classic denim blue jeans` can belong to both the `Woman's > Blue Jeans` and `Classic collection` categories at the same time.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * The tag data type is not supported for custom labels.
>   * The tag value must match the product data feed exactly.
> 


The following operators are supported for product category:

Operator (AIQUA dashboard)| Operator (API call)| Description  
---|---|---  
`is any of`| `in`| The data feed value includes at least one of the filtering values.**Example** The data feed value is `Woman's > Blue Jeans` and `Classic Collection`.If the filter value is: • `Woman's > blue jeans` → Match • `classic collection` → Match • `Blue Jeans` → Not a match  
`is not`| `nin`| The data feed value does not include any of the filtering values.  
`contains`| `contains`| The data feed value contains and partially matches at least one of the filtering values.**Example** The data feed value is `Woman's > Pants > Blue Jeans`.If the filter value is: • `Blue Jeans` → Match • `pants` → Match • `Woman's > Pants` → Match • `Woman's > Blue Jeans` → Not a match  
`does not contain`| `not contains`| The data feed value doesn't contain any exact matches with the filtering values.  
  
### 

Float

The following operators are supported for `originalPrice`, `price` (Discounted Price), and custom labels with the float data type.

Operator (AIQUA dashboard)| Operator (API call)| Description  
---|---|---  
`>`| `gt`| Greater than  
`>=`| `gte`| Greater than or equal to  
`=`| `eq`| Equal to  
`<=`| `lte`| Less than or equal to  
`<`| `lt`| Less than  
`!=`| `ne`| Not equal to  
`between`| `between`| Between two numbers  
  
### 

Boolean

For custom labels with the data type set to boolean, you can set the condition to `true` or `false` on the AIQUA dashboard.

![](https://files.readme.io/e3a0347f6a2a4cbce6e105f88b9a96e33ff289112a479cec927a383369c066c0-scenario-product-filter-boolean-value.png)

In API calls, pass in the `eq` operator.

Operator (API calls)| Description  
---|---  
`eq`| Equal to

# Implementing Deep Links

## 

Overview

The Appier Flutter SDK supports general deep link routing across all SDK versions. The SDK does not resolve or handle deep links directly. Instead, it passes them to your app for processing. Starting from SDK version 3.2.0, you can call `handleUriOpened()` to enable to track clicks on deep links.

* * *

## 

1\. Native implementation

To implement basic deep link routing, refer to the instructions for each platform:

  * Android deep links
  * iOS deep links



### 

Android deep links

Follow the [deep link implementation instructions for Android](doc:implementing-deep-links-for-android).

### 

iOS deep links

Deep links on iOS can be implemented using one of the following methods:

  * Option 1: Using a custom URL scheme
  * Option 2: Using universal links



#### 

Option 1: Using a custom URL scheme

Follow the [deep link implementation instructions for iOS](doc:implementing-deep-links-for-ios#option-1-using-a-custom-url-scheme).

#### 

Option 2: Using universal links

Call `setUniversalLinkDomains()` after `AppierFlutter.configure()`:

Dart
    
    
    @override
      void initState() {
        super.initState();
        AppierFlutter.configure(
          '<APP_ID>',
          appGroup: '<iOS_APP_GROUP>',
        );
        AppierFlutter.setUniversalLinkDomains(["YOUR_DOMAIN_1", "YOUR_DOMAIN_2"]);
      }

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important
> 
> To prevent unexpected issues, don't call `setUniversalLinkDomains()` in the native iOS code.

After setting up native deep link routing, you can optionally implement deep link tracking to track clicks on deep links.

* * *

## 

2\. (Optional) Implementing deep link tracking

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Supported version
> 
>   * Flutter SDK 3.2.0 or later
> 


To track clicks on a deep link, pass the deep link into `handleUriOpened()`. When `handleUriOpened()` is called, the SDK automatically logs an `aiq_deep_link_redirected` event.

Dart
    
    
    static Future<void> handleUriOpened(String uriString)

### 

`aiq_deep_link_redirected` event parameters

Name| Type| Description| Always included  
---|---|---|---  
`url`| String| The deep link URL.| Yes  
`last_app_launched_time`| Number| The last app launch timestamp. `0` if the app hasn't launched before.| Yes  
`timestamp`| Number| The timestamp when the deep link is triggered.| Yes  
`utm_id`| String| The campaign ID (comma-separated).| No  
`utm_term`| String| The paid search keyword (comma-separated).| No  
`utm_campaign`| String| The campaign or promotion name (comma-separated).| No  
`utm_medium`| String| The medium or channel (such as `email`, `cpc`) (comma-separated).| No  
`utm_source`| String| The source of traffic (such as `Google`, `Facebook`) (comma-separated).| No  
`utm_content`| String| The differentiator for similar ads or links (comma-separated).| No  
`utm_source_platform`| String| The platform that directs traffic (such as `Search Ads 360`) (comma-separated).| No  
`utm_creative_format`| String| The creative type (such as `video`, `display`) (comma-separated).| No  
`utm_marketing_tactic`| String| The targeting method (such as `remarketing`) (comma-separated).| No  
`asi`| String| The Appier click ID (comma-separated).| No  
  
### 

Example

The following code sample demonstrates how to implement deep link tracking, using the [`app_links`](https://pub.dev/packages/app_links) package to handle deep links and [`firebase_messaging`](https://pub.dev/packages/firebase_messaging) package to handle push notifications.

dart
    
    
    import 'package:firebase_messaging/firebase_messaging.dart';
    import 'package:app_links/app_links.dart';
    import 'package:appier_flutter/appier_flutter.dart';
    
    class DeepLinkHandler {
      // Best practice: Store the last handled URI to prevent duplicate events
      String? _lastHandledUri;
    
      // Processes the incoming deep link URI
      void handleUri(String uri) {
        // Avoid handling the same URI multiple times
        if (_lastHandledUri == uri) return;
    
        _lastHandledUri = uri;
    
        // Best practice: Call handleUriOpened() as soon as the link is available
        AppierFlutter.handleUriOpened(uri);
      }
    
      Future<void> initializeDeepLinks() async {
        final appLinks = AppLinks();
    
        // Entry point 1: Deep link on cold start (app was not running)
        final initialLink = await appLinks.getInitialLink();
        if (initialLink != null) {
          final uriStr = initialLink.toString();
          print("Initial deep link received: $uriStr");
          handleUri(uriStr);
        }
    
        // Entry point 2: Deep link while app is in background or foreground
        appLinks.uriLinkStream.listen((Uri? uri) {
          if (uri != null) {
            final uriStr = uri.toString();
            print("Deep link received while app running: $uriStr");
            handleUri(uriStr);
          }
        });
    
        // Entry point 3: Deep link from Firebase push notification
        FirebaseMessaging.onMessageOpenedApp.listen((message) {
          final link = message.data['deep_link'];
          if (link != null) {
            print('Deep link from push notification: $link');
            handleUri(link);
          }
        });
      }
    }
    
    // Usage example:
    // final deepLinkHandler = DeepLinkHandler();
    // await deepLinkHandler.initializeDeepLinks();

# Flutter In-App Inbox Campaigns

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> In-app inbox campaigns are a beta feature. While this feature is currently available for use, you may encounter occasional bugs or stability issues.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Prerequisites
> 
>   * Complete the [Appier Flutter SDK integration](doc:flutter-sdk-integration-overview).
>   * [Create an in-app campaign](doc:campaigns-in-app-create) on the AIQUA dashboard with the campaign type set to **Inbox**.
> 


In-app inbox campaigns allow you to fetch campaigns from AIQUA and store them on local device storage. You can choose how and when to display these locally-stored campaigns to app users without having to rely on push campaigns or pop-up campaigns.

## 

Inbox vs pop-up and push campaigns

Inbox campaigns differ from [pop-up campaigns](doc:in-app-popup-notifications-for-ios-sdk) and [push campaigns](doc:push-notification-guide-for-ios) in several ways. Namely, inbox campaigns can be:

  * **Fetched using an SDK method** : Fetch new campaigns using `fetchInboxMessages()`. Other campaign types can't be fetched with SDK methods. Instead, they are received by the device after AIQUA delivers the campaign.
  * **Delivered silently** : Other campaign types are displayed to the user as soon as the campaign is delivered. With inbox campaigns, you can silently retrieve campaigns and choose how and when to display the locally-stored notifications to app users.
  * **Stored on the device** : On every app launch, the SDK fetches and stores the latest campaigns in the inbox using the device's local storage. Stored inbox campaigns can then be retrieved from local device storage using `getInboxMessages()`.



### 

Logging events for inbox campaigns

The Flutter SDK doesn't automatically log impression and click events for inbox campaigns. To view in-app inbox campaign performance data on the AIQUA dashboard, inbox campaign impression and click events must be logged manually using `logEvent()`.

* * *

## 

Example use case: In-app message center

Using inbox campaigns, we'd like to implement a message center in our app. The message center will contain messages notifying our users of app updates and product announcements. We're using inbox campaigns for this feature so that:

  * We can receive new messages without interrupting the user, since inbox campaigns are retrieved silently by default.
  * Messages are stored in the inbox using local device storage, so users can choose to view the messages at any time by navigating to the app's message center.



### 

In-app message center: Implementation

To use the Flutter SDK methods to implement the message center described above, follow these steps:

Step| Description  
---|---  
1| (Optional) Change the message capacity of the inbox in your app using `updateInboxRecordLimit()`.By default, the inbox capacity is set to 50.  
2| When the app is launched, new inbox campaigns are automatically fetched from AIQUA. These campaigns will be stored on the device for later retrieval.You can a call `fetchInboxMessages()` at any time to retrieve the latest inbox campaigns.  
3| When a user navigates to the message center, get a list of all locally-stored messages to display on the screen using `getInboxMessages()`.  
4| (Optional) Log a `qg_inapp_displayed` event for each displayed message.Logging this event will allow you to view this campaign performance metric on the AIQUA dashboard.  
5| 

  * When a user clicks on a message in the message center, retrieve that message's contents from the array returned by `getInboxMessages()` and display it to the user.
  * After a message has been read, update the message's status to `READ` using `setStatus()`.

  
6| (Optional) Log a `qg_inapp_clicked` event for the clicked message.Logging this event will allow you to view this campaign performance metric on the AIQUA dashboard.  
  
### 

In-app message center: Force refresh feature

In our message center, we want to include a force refresh button that a user can click to fetch the latest messages. To accomplish this, we'll employ the following SDK methods:

  * `fetchInboxMessages()`: Fetches new messages from AIQUA's servers and saves them locally.
  * `getInboxMessages()`: Returns a list of all locally-stored campaigns.



The following code sample demonstrates how to implement a force refresh:

Kotlin
    
    
    // Fetch the latest inbox campaigns from AIQUA's servers
    AppierFlutter.fetchInboxMessages(AsyncResult(onSuccess:(value) {}, onError: (error) {}));
    
    // Get the list of all the locally-stored campaigns
    List<Message> myInboxMessages = AppierFlutter.getInboxMessages(true, true, false);

* * *

## 

`Message`

Each inbox campaign is an instance of the `Message` class and contains the following properties:

Name| Type| Description  
---|---|---  
`notificationId`| `int`| The in-app campaign ID.  
`title`| `String`| The campaign title.  
`image`| `String`| The campaign image URL.  
`text`| `String`| The campaign message.  
`deepLink`| `String`| The campaign deep link.  
`startTime`| `int`| The campaign's start time.  
`endTime`| `int`| The campaign's end time.  
`status`| `MessageStatus`| The status of the message—either `read`, `unread`, or `deleted`.  
`parameters`| `Map<String, dynamic>`| The [key-value pairs](doc:flutter-receiving-key-value-pairs) included in the campaign.  
  
### 

`MessageStatus`

The `MessageStatus` enum defines the possible states for a `Message` (inbox campaign):

Dart
    
    
    enum MessageStatus {
      unread,
      read,
      deleted
    }

* * *

## 

In-app inbox campaign methods

Use the following class methods to implement inbox campaigns in your app:

  * `updateInboxRecordLimit()`: Set the maximum number of campaigns to store locally.
  * `fetchInboxMessages()`: Fetch inbox campaigns from AIQUA.
  * `getInboxMessages()`: Get locally-stored inbox campaigns.
  * `setStatus()`: Set the status of an inbox campaign.
  * `logEvent()`: Logging impressions and click events for an inbox campaign.



### 

`updateInboxRecordLimit()`

Dart
    
    
    void updateInboxRecordLimit(int maxAmount)

Sets the maximum number of campaigns to store locally. By default, the maximum capacity is set to 50 notifications.

Please note that the following operations can potentially delete locally stored campaigns:

  * If the number of stored campaigns exceeds the storage limit while fetching new campaigns, the oldest campaigns will be deleted.
  * If you change the storage limit to a size smaller than the number of currently stored campaigns, the oldest notification will be deleted.



For example, the following line limits the number of locally-stored inbox messages to 100.

Dart
    
    
    AppierFlutter.updateInboxRecordLimit(100);

### 

`fetchInboxMessages()`

Dart
    
    
    void fetchInboxMessages(AsyncResult<void> asyncResult)

An asynchronous method that fetches new inbox campaigns from AIQUA's servers and saves them locally as a list of `Message` objects, then activates a completion handler notifying of the success or failure of the operation:

Dart
    
    
    // Fetch in-app inbox campaigns
    AppierFlutter.fetchInboxMessages(AsyncResult(onSuccess:(value) {}, onError: (error) {}));

### 

`getInboxMessages()`

Dart
    
    
    List<Message> getInboxMessages(bool read, bool unread, bool deleted)

A synchronous method that returns a list of `Message` objects representing locally-stored inbox campaigns, ordered by campaign priority. The function parameters are as follows:

Name| Description  
---|---  
`read`| • `true`: Include inbox campaigns with the status "Read"   
• `false`: Exclude inbox campaigns with the status "Read"  
`unread`| • `true`: Include inbox campaigns with the status "Unread"   
• `false`: Exclude inbox campaigns with the status "Unread"  
`deleted`| • `true`: Include inbox campaigns with the status "Deleted"   
• `false`: Exclude inbox campaigns with the status "Deleted"  
  
> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> Although the latest inbox messages are fetched whenever the app is launched, you should call `fetchInboxMessages()` before calling `getInboxMessages()` if you want to retrieve the latest messages from AIQUA's servers.

Return a list of inbox campaigns depending on the notification's status. For example, you can make the following method call to get list of all inbox campaigns that have been read and unread, but not deleted.

Dart
    
    
    List<Message> myInboxMessages = AppierFlutter.getInboxMessages(true, true, false);

### 

`setStatus()`

Dart
    
    
    void setStatus(Status status)

Updates the notification's status using one of the values defined in the `MessageStatus` enum. For example, if the user reads, then deletes a message, the status flags can be updated using two calls to `setStatus()`:

Dart
    
    
    message.setStatus(MessageStatus.read)

### 

`logEvent()`

Dart
    
    
    void logEvent(String eventName, Map<String, dynamic>? info)

Use `logEvent()` to log the following types of event for inbox campaigns:

  * Custom events
  * Campaign performance events (clicks and impressions) that you want to view on the AIQUA dashboard



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> When logging any event for an inbox notification, the notification's `notificationId` is automatically added as an event parameter by the Appier SDK.

#### 

Logging custom events

When using `logEvent()` to log custom events, include any additional event parameters as defined in your custom event schema.

The following code sample retrieves all read inbox messages, then logs a custom event with a parameter for the first message:

Dart
    
    
    message.logEvent('custom_event', { "key1": "value1", "key2": "value2"})

#### 

Logging campaign performance events

To track and view impressions and clicks on the AIQUA dashboard, you need to manually log the following events using `logEvent()`:

  * `qg_inapp_displayed` for impressions
  * `qg_inapp_clicked` for clicks



> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Tip
> 
> You don't need to add event parameters when logging `qg_inapp_displayed` or `qg_inapp_clicked`.

Dart
    
    
    message.logEvent('qg_inapp_displayed', {})

Although these events are [default events](doc:default-aiqua-parameters), the Appier SDK doesn't automatically log them for inbox campaigns. When properly logged, these performance metrics are visible from the [in-app campaign list](doc:campaigns-in-app-manage#campaign-list-metrics).

# Native Push Setup

### 

Android

The Appier SDK will automatically handles push notifications for Android apps. No additional setup is required.

If you have special requirements such as requiring the use of multiple Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) services, using custom FCM services, or your want to disable push notifications from AIQUA, you can customize your own FCM service, [customize the native `FirebaseMessagingService` class](doc:push-notifications-for-android#custom-firebasemessagingservice-implementation).

### 

iOS

#### 

Prerequisites

Before configuring push notifications for iOS, complete the following:

  * [Configure iOS credentials](doc:creating-push-certificates)
  * [Enable capabilities](doc:enabling-capabilities)



#### 

Required steps

Complete the following steps to send push notifications:

  1. Complete steps 1-3 and step 4A in [Registering for Push Notifications](doc:registering-push-notifications-for-ios)
  2. [Handle push notifications](doc:handling-push-notifications-for-ios)
  3. [Configure rich push notifications](doc:rich-push-notifications-for-flutter)
  4. [Implement deep links](doc:flutter-deep-links)



#### 

Apps using Firebase Cloud Messaging

For Flutter apps using FCM to send push notifications, developers should set the delegate of `UNUserNotificationCenter` for iOS 10 or later. For more details, see [Registering for Push Notifications](doc:registering-push-notifications-for-ios#3-requesting-permission).

# Flutter SDK Integration Overview

## 

Overview

Integrate your app with Appier Flutter SDK to take advantage of features such as sending push notifications, logging custom user data, and delivering in-app campaigns. This page summarizes the setup steps required to begin using the Appier Flutter SDK and all the features it supports.

### 

Latest Appier SDK version

We recommend using the latest Appier Flutter SDK for continual updates and feature support. See the [Flutter SDK Release Notes](doc:flutter-sdk-release-notes) for details about the latest releases.

Latest Appier Flutter SDK version| SDK download  
---|---  
3.5.1| [Flutter Plugin for Appier Enterprise Solutions](https://pub.dev/packages/appier_flutter)  
  
### 

Dependencies

The Appier Flutter SDK is built with the following `environment` and `dependencies`:

Appier Flutter SDK 3.0.0 or laterAppier Flutter SDK 2.8.0 or earlier
    
    
    environment:
      sdk: ">=2.17.0 <4.0.0"
      flutter: ">=3.0.0"
    
    dependencies:
      flutter:
        sdk: flutter
      flutter_inappwebview: ^6.1.5
    
    
    environment:
      sdk: ">=2.12.0 <3.0.0"
      flutter: ">=1.20.0"
    
    dependencies:
      flutter:
        sdk: flutter
      flutter_inappwebview: ^5.0.5

### 

Pre-release versions (testing only)

Any Appier Flutter SDK version with `alpha`, `beta`, `rc`, in the version number are testing versions or release candidates. These pre-release versions may be unstable and are intended for testing purposes.

* * *

## 

Integration overview

Integrating your app with Appier Flutter SDK allows you to utilize the following features:

  * Send push notifications
  * Send in-app campaigns
  * Track user events and attributes



You need to complete the following steps.

  1. [Installing the SDK via pub.dev](doc:installing-the-sdk-via-flutter)
  2. [Required Setup for Native Android and iOS](doc:initial-setup-for-native-android-and-ios-for-flutter)

# Stable Flutter SDK Versions

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note: Known issues
> 
> This page only announces critical known issues and their fixes. Issues are classified as critical if they cause campaign failures or app crashes that are highly likely to be encountered by app users.
> 
> For a comprehensive list of known issues and bug fixes, please refer to the native SDK release notes ([Android](doc:release-notes-android), [iOS](doc:release-notes-ios)).

# 

v3.0.0 - September 13, 2024

### 

Changed

  * The Appier Flutter SDK now uses `InAppWebView` version 6.0.0. If your app uses web views and you're upgrading to this version of the Appier SDK, please follow the instructions in the [`InAppWebView` migration guide](https://inappwebview.dev/docs/migration-guide/).
  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.25.0 to 7.26.0. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.33.0 to 7.34.0. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



* * *

# 

v2.8.0 - August 2, 2024

### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.24.3 to 7.25.0. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.32.3 to 7.33.0. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



* * *

# 

v2.7.0 - April 12, 2024

### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.24.0 to 7.24.3. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.32.1 to 7.32.3. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



* * *

# 

v2.6.0 - March 1, 2024

### 

New

  * In compliance with Apple's [new privacy updates for App Store submissions](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=r1henawx), the Appier SDK now provides:
    * A privacy manifest: The privacy manifest includes a property list of all the types of data collected by the SDK, and the reasons for certain API usage. For details, see [Apple App Privacy](doc:apple-app-privacy#app-privacy-manifest-ios-sdk-7320-or-later).
    * Code signing: The XCFramework is now signed by Appier, ensuring that your app is using a secure SDK.
  * Support for in-app creative studio. To learn more about this beta feature, contact your customer success manager.



### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.23.1 to 7.24.0. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.30.2 to 7.32.1. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
    * Note that IDFA is no longer collected by default.



* * *

# 

v2.5.1 - December 29, 2023

### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.23.0 to 7.23.1. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.30.0 to 7.30.2. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



* * *

# 

v2.5.0 - November 24, 2023

### 

New

  * Introduced geofencing. To learn more about this beta feature, contact your customer success manager.
  * Added [user data permission controls](doc:flutter-user-data-permission-controls) for AAID, IDFA, and location data.



### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.22.0 to 7.23.0. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.29.0 to 7.30.0. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Changed the handler function for routing push messages to Appier SDK with `firebase_messaging` plugin. To use geofencing or silent push notifications with `firebase_messaging` plugin, please [reconfigure the function](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/flutter-using-the-firebase-messaging-plugin#3-route-messages-to-the-appier-sdk).



### 

Fixed

  * [Requesting recommendations](doc:recommendation-web) in a web view caused a JSON syntax error.



### 

Known issues

  * (iOS only) Potential app crashes when configuring [user data permission controls](doc:flutter-user-data-permission-controls) in debug mode
  * (iOS only) [User data permission controls](doc:flutter-user-data-permission-controls) configured before SDK initialization might not take effect for first-installed apps
  * (iOS only) Apps using `UISceneDelegate` are required to do additional implementations



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note: Known issues
> 
> Please contact Appier Support for more details and ways to work around these issues.

* * *

# 

v2.4.0 - October 20, 2023

### 

New

  * Support for [stored push notifications](doc:flutter-storing-push-notifications).



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note: Geofencing
> 
> To use geofencing, please refer to Flutter SDK 2.5.0. While geofencing is supported in the bridged iOS and Android SDK versions, this feature is untested in Flutter SDK 2.4.0.

### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from 7.20.0 to 7.22.0. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from 7.27.0 to 7.29.0. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Revamped the implementation of [Small, Medium, and Full Screen in-app pop-up creatives](doc:campaigns-in-app-popup-basic-creatives) for visual consistency across mobile platforms.



### 

Known issues

  * [Requesting recommendations](doc:recommendation-web) in a web view caused a JSON syntax error.
    * Note: While this issue has been fixed in the bridged Android and iOS SDK versions, it has not yet been fixed in Flutter SDK 2.4.0.



* * *

# 

v2.3.0 - July 21, 2023

### 

Fixed

  * The Flutter SDK returned an error message when retrieving recommendations in a web view if the `num` parameter was an `int` value.



### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from `7.17.2` to `7.20.0`. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from `7.24.0` to `7.27.0`. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



* * *

# 

v2.2.0 - May 12, 2023

### 

New

  * Support for the [Display background overlay](doc:campaigns-in-app-popup-basic-creatives#background-overlay) option to display or disable the background overlay for in-app notifications.
  * Support for syncing LINE users with app users via a URL in AIQUA LINE campaigns that lands on the SDK-integrated app or via a LIFF URL. For details, see [LINE User Profile Sync](doc:campaigns-getting-started-line-user-sync).
    * Note that the iOS SDK uses [method swizzling](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling) to support LINE user profile sync by default. Method swizzling may cause [conflicts with third-party SDKs](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#sdk-conflicts) resulting in app crashes. If your app uses third-party SDKs that conflict with iOS SDK, you can [disable method swizzling](doc:ios-sdk-method-swizzling#disabling-method-swizzling) and manually enable LINE user profile sync.



### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from `7.10.0` to `7.17.2`. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from `7.18.0` to `7.24.0`. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



* * *

# 

v2.1.1 - March 24, 2023

### 

Fixed

  * Executing the `flutter build apk` command would fail with an error due to incompatibilities with certain third-party Android libraries.

v2.1.0 - September 16, 2022

### 

New

  * Support for configurable [on-click behavior](doc:campaigns-in-app-popup-basic-creatives#click-behavior) for in-app pop-up campaign floating icons.



### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from `7.9.1` to `7.10.0`. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from `7.17.0` to `7.18.0`. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.



### 

Fixed

  * The `app_launched` event wasn’t logged when launching the app:
    * For the first time after being installed
    * After the app was killed by the user or OS



* * *

# 

v2.0.0 - July 22, 2022

### 

New

  * Support for regenerating users via [`renewUserId()`](https://pub.dev/documentation/appier_flutter/latest/appier_flutter/AppierFlutter/renewUserId.html).
  * Support for the `firebase_messaging` plugin. For instructions on using this plugin to set up push notifications, see [Using the Firebase Messaging Plugin](doc:flutter-using-the-firebase-messaging-plugin).



### 

Changed

  * Updated the bridged Appier Android SDK version from `7.3.1` to `7.9.1`. See the [Android SDK release notes](doc:android-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.
  * Updated the bridged Appier iOS SDK version from `7.13.0` to `7.17.0`. See the [iOS SDK release notes](doc:ios-sdk-release-notes) for a detailed summary of changes.

# Storing Push Notifications

The Appier Flutter SDK allows you to enable push notification storage, and provides APIs for the following operations:

  * Setting the maximum notification storage limit
  * Retrieving stored notifications
  * Deleting stored notifications



## 

Requirements and limitations

  * Your app must be using Flutter SDK 2.4.0 or later
  * The Appier SDK can only store notifications sent by AIQUA



* * *

## 

Enabling stored notifications

Push notification storage is disabled by default. To enable it, call `enableStoredNotifications()`.

Dart
    
    
    AppierFlutter.enableStoredNotifications();

* * *

## 

Setting the notification storage limit

By default, the notification storage limit is set to 20. Messages that exceed the storage limit are deleted, with the oldest messages being deleted first.

Use `setStoredNotificationsLimit()` to change the storage limit. In the following example, the storage limit is set to 3:

Dart
    
    
    AppierFlutter.setStoredNotificationsLimit(3);

* * *

## 

Retrieving stored notifications

`getStoredNotifications()` returns a JSON array of the notifications and their fields.

Dart
    
    
    AppierFlutter.getStoredNotifications().then((data) {
      // handle the retrieved data
    });

Different types of notifications may include different fields. However, all of them have a `title` and a `message`. They may also have `imageUrl`, `bigImageUrl`, `deepLink` and other fields depending on the notification type. For details on image specifications, refer to the following pages:

  * [Android push creatives](doc:creatives-android-push)
  * [iOS push creatives](doc:creatives-ios-push)



* * *

## 

Deleting stored notifications

### 

Deleting a single notification

You can delete a single notification by retrieving it's position in the array returned by `getStoredNotifications()` and passing it into `deleteStoredNotification()`. The following example deleted the first stored notification (at position 0) in the array:

Dart
    
    
    AppierFlutter.deleteStoredNotification(0);

For example, you can use `deleteNotificationAtIndex()` to delete a notification from the app's notification history after a user reads or clicks it.

### 

Deleting all notifications

Delete all locally stored AIQUA notifications using `deleteAllStoreNotifications()`:

Dart
    
    
    AppierFlutter.deleteAllStoredNotifications();

# Troubleshooting Dependency Conflicts

If you're using one of the libraries listed below, follow the instructions provided on this page to resolve dependency conflicts with the Appier SDK:

  * Google Analytics API for Firebase (Android)
  * Firebase Messaging (Android)
  * Firebase BoM (Android)



> 👍
> 
> ### 
> 
> Android SDK dependencies
> 
> Refer to the [Android SDK's dependencies](doc:sdk-android-dependencies) to ensure that they don't conflict with your app's other dependencies.

### 

Google Analytics API for Firebase (Android)

The [Google Analytics API for Firebase](https://firebase.google.com/docs/analytics/) conflicts with the Appier Android SDK's `com.google.android.gms:play-services-analytics` dependency.

If your project uses the Google Analytics API, append the following configuration to `android/app/build.gradle` to resolve this dependency conflict:

Groovy
    
    
    configurations.all { conf ->
        conf.dependencies.all { dep ->
            if (dep.name == 'appier_flutter') {
                dep.exclude group: 'com.google.android.gms'
                dependencies {
                    implementation 'com.google.android.gms:play-services-ads-identifier:16.0.0'
                }
            }
        }
    }

The configuration above includes the `play-services-ads-identifier:16.0.0` dependency required by the Appier Android SDK and excludes `com.google.android.gms`.

### 

Firebase Messaging (Android)

The Appier Android SDK uses `firebase-messaging` version 17.3.4. If your app uses a different version, update `android/app/build.gradle` to exclude the version used by the Appier SDK, then include the version that your app uses. Additionally, if you are using version 22.0.0 or later, you'll need to include the `com.google.firebase:firebase-iid:20.0.1` dependency as well.

To use a different version of `firebase-messaging` in your app, append the following configuration to `android/app/build.gradle`:

Groovy
    
    
    configurations.all { conf ->
        conf.dependencies.all { dep ->
            if (dep.name == 'appier_flutter') {
                dep.exclude group: 'com.google.firebase'
                dependencies {
                    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging:<YOUR VERSION NUMBER>'
    
                    // If you're using firebase-messaging version 22.0.0+, add this line as well. 
                    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-iid:20.0.1'
                }
            }
        }
    }

### 

Firebase BoM (Android)

If you're using `firebase-bom` version 8.0.0 or later, you'll need to exclude the Appier Android SDK's `com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging:17.3.4` dependency and include the `com.google.firebase:firebase-iid:20.0.1` dependency.

To resolve this dependency conflict, append the following configuration to `android/app/build.gradle`:

Groovy
    
    
    configurations.all { conf ->
        conf.dependencies.all { dep ->
            if (dep.name == 'appier_flutter') {
                dep.exclude group: 'com.google.firebase'
                dependencies {
                    implementation platform('com.google.firebase:firebase-bom:<your-version>')
                    implementation 'com.google.firebase:firebase-iid:20.0.1'
                }
            }
        }
    }

# Flutter User Data Permission Controls

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Required SDK version
> 
> User data permissions controls are only available on Flutter SDK 2.5.0 or later. See known issues in Flutter [here](https://docs.aiqua.appier.com/docs/flutter-sdk-release-notes#known-issues).

## 

Overview

To allow your app to comply with data privacy policies and regulations, the Appier Flutter SDK allows you to manage user data permissions for the following types of data:

  * **Google Advertising ID (AAID)** : Collection is enabled by default.
  * **Identifier for Advertising (IDFA)**
    * Flutter SDK 3.2.0 or later: IDFA collection is disabled by default.
      * Known issue for Flutter SDK 2.6.0 to 3.1.1: If passing a `DataTrackingConfig` instance into `setDataTrackingConfig()` without explicitly setting `collectIdfa`, `collectIdfa` will be set to `true`.
    * For Flutter SDK 2.5.1 and earlier: IDFA collection is enabled by default.
  * **Location data** : Collection is disabled by default.



You can enable or disable collection for this data at any point in your app's lifecycle, even before the Appier SDK is initialized, by passing a`DataTrackingConfig` object into `setDataTrackingConfig()`and the changes will be effective immediately. For example, you may want to update user data collection settings in the following scenarios:

  * After the app is launched.
  * After a user has responded to a data collection consent prompt.
  * After [regenerating the user's Appier ID](https://pub.dev/documentation/appier_flutter/latest/appier_flutter/AppierFlutter/renewAppierId.html).
  * After a user logs in or logs out of their account.



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> To ensure user privacy and avoid unintended data collection, we recommend disabling AAID and IDFA collection before initializing the Appier SDK.
> 
> The default settings for AAID and IDFA collection across different Flutter SDK versions are as follows:
> 
> Flutter SDK version| AAID| IDFA  
> ---|---|---  
> 2.5.1 and earlier| Collected by default.| Collected by default.  
> 2.6.0 or later| Collected by default.| Not collected by default.  
  
* * *

## 

`DataTrackingConfig` object

The `DataTrackingConfig` object contains the SDK's current data permissions settings. The default settings for the latest SDK version are as follows:

Dart
    
    
    class DataTrackingConfig {
      bool collectLocation = false;   // Location data collection disabled by default
      bool collectAaid = true;        // AAID collection enabled by default 
      bool collectIdfa = false;       // IDFA collection disabled by default
    }

* * *

## 

Retrieving data permissions settings

Use `getDataTrackingConfig()` to retrieve the current data permission settings.

Dart
    
    
    final currentConfig = await AppierFlutter.getDataTrackingConfig();
    
    // currentConfig contains all of the user data permission settings
    final currentIdfaConfig = currentConfig.collectIdfa;
    final currentAaidConfig = currentConfig.collectAaid;
    final currentLocationConfig = currentConfig.collectLocation;

* * *

## 

Setting data permission settings

To set all data permissions simultaneously, instantiate a `DataTrackingConfig` instance and pass it into `setDataTrackingConfig()`.

Dart
    
    
    // Instantiate a new DataTrackingConfig object with custom settings
    final newConfig = DataTrackingConfig(collectLocation: false, collectAaid: true, collectIdfa: false)
    
    // Apply the custom data permission settings
    await AppierFlutter.setDataTrackingConfig(newConfig);

# Using the Firebase Messaging Plugin

## 

Overview

The Appier SDK supports the `firebase_messaging` plugin to enable push notifications for both the Android and iOS platforms. For more information about the `firebase_messaging` plugin, see [Flutter’s Cloud Messaging](https://firebase.flutter.dev/docs/messaging/overview/) docs.

  1. Complete the prerequisites.
  2. Follow the push setup steps for Android and iOS.



* * *

### 

Prerequisites for using the `firebase_messaging` plugin

Before proceeding with the push notification setup, complete the following steps in your Flutter project:

  * [Add Firebase](https://firebase.google.com/docs/flutter/setup?platform=android) to your Flutter app. Complete the instructions for both [Android](https://firebase.google.com/docs/flutter/setup?platform=android) and [iOS](https://firebase.google.com/docs/flutter/setup?platform=ios).
  * [Install the `firebase_messaging` plugin](https://firebase.flutter.dev/docs/messaging/overview/#installation).



* * *

## 

Push notification setup for Android devices

### 

1\. Register app info with AIQUA

Complete the steps to [register your Android app with AIQUA](doc:entering-app-info-on-aiqua-dashboard).

### 

2\. Set up message handling

Follow the instructions in the Flutter guides listed below to allow your app to handle incoming messages:

  * [Handling foreground messages](https://firebase.flutter.dev/docs/messaging/usage/#foreground-messages)
  * [Handling background messages](https://firebase.flutter.dev/docs/messaging/usage/#background-messages)



### 

3\. Route messages to the Appier SDK

  1. Define a function for handling both background and foreground messages:



Dart
    
    
    /// This handler can handle normal and silent pushes.
    @pragma(‘vm:entry-point’)
    Future<void> _handleFcmMessage(RemoteMessage message) async {
      final from = message.from;
      final data = message.data;
      final dataString = jsonEncode(data);
      final isAppierPush = await AppierFlutter.isAppierPush(dataString);
      if (from != null && isAppierPush) {
        await AppierFlutter.handleRemoteMessage(dataString);
      }
    }

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> This function was changed in Flutter SDK 2.5.0 to support geofencing and silent push notifications.
> 
> If you have set up push notifications with Firebase Messaging Plugin before Flutter SDK 2.5.0 and would like to use these features, please reconfigure this step.

  2. Connect foreground messages to the handler function:



Dart
    
    
    FirebaseMessaging.onMessage.listen((message) {
      ...
      _handleFcmMessage(message);
      ...
    });

  3. Connect background messages to the handler function:



Dart
    
    
    Future<void> _firebaseMessagingBackgroundHandler(RemoteMessage message) async {
      ...
      await _handleFcmMessage(message);
      ...
    }
    ...
    FirebaseMessaging.onBackgroundMessage(_firebaseMessagingBackgroundHandler);
    ...

### 

4\. Send a test push campaign

[Send a test push campaign](doc:test-notification-for-android) to verify that your push notification implementation is correct.

* * *

## 

Push notification setup for iOS devices

### 

1\. Configure your APNS credentials on FCM

Follow the instructions listed in [Configuring Push Credentials](doc:creating-push-certificates) to generate APNs credentials.

### 

2\. Provide FCM tokens to the Appier SDK

Get the FCM token by calling `FirebaseMessaging.instance.getToken()`, then provide it to Appier SDK using `setFcmToken()`:

Swift
    
    
    final token = await FirebaseMessaging.instance.getToken();
    if (token != null) {
      await AppierFlutter.setFcmToken(token);
    }

### 

3\. Request push permission and enable foreground notifications

Follow the Flutter guides listed below request push permission and enable foreground notifications:

  * [Requesting push permission for iOS](https://firebase.flutter.dev/docs/messaging/usage/#requesting-permission-apple--web)
  * [Enabling foreground notifications for iOS](https://firebase.flutter.dev/docs/messaging/notifications/#ios-configuration)



### 

4\. Enable capabilities

Follow [this Flutter guide](https://firebase.flutter.dev/docs/messaging/apple-integration/#configuring-your-app) to enable the "Push Notifications" and "Background Modes" capabilities in Xcode.

### 

5\. Bridge notification handling in `AppDelegate.swift`

Open your native iOS Xcode project workspace by navigating to your project project directory and running the following command:

Shell
    
    
    open ios/Runner.xcworkspace

Find your `AppDelegate.swift` file. The original `AppDelegate.swift` generated by flutter will look like this:

Swift
    
    
    import UIKit
    import Flutter
    
    @UIApplicationMain
    @objc class AppDelegate: FlutterAppDelegate {
      override func application(
        _ application: UIApplication,
        didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey: Any]?
      ) -> Bool {
        GeneratedPluginRegistrant.register(with: self)
        return super.application(application, didFinishLaunchingWithOptions: launchOptions)
      }
    }

  1. First, add `import Appier` under `import Flutter` and `UNUserNotificationCenter.current().delegate = self` under `GeneratedPluginRegistrant.register(with: self)`:



Swift
    
    
    import UIKit
    import Flutter
    import Appier
    
    @UIApplicationMain
    @objc class AppDelegate: FlutterAppDelegate {
      override func application(
        _ application: UIApplication,
        didFinishLaunchingWithOptions launchOptions: [UIApplication.LaunchOptionsKey: Any]?
      ) -> Bool {
        GeneratedPluginRegistrant.register(with: self)
        UNUserNotificationCenter.current().delegate = self
        return super.application(application, didFinishLaunchingWithOptions: launchOptions)
      }
    }

  2. Next, override these three methods in the `AppDelegate`:


  * `application(_:didReceiveRemoteNotification:fetchCompletionHandler:)`
  * `userNotificationCenter(_:didReceive:withCompletionHandler)`
  * `userNotificationCenter(_:willPresent:withCompletionHandler:)`



Swift
    
    
    @objc class AppDelegate: FlutterAppDelegate {
      ...
      override func application(_ application: UIApplication, didReceiveRemoteNotification userInfo: [AnyHashable : Any], fetchCompletionHandler completionHandler: @escaping (UIBackgroundFetchResult) -> Void) {
        QGSdk.getSharedInstance().application(application, didReceiveRemoteNotification: userInfo)
        super.application(application, didReceiveRemoteNotification: userInfo, fetchCompletionHandler: completionHandler)
      }
    
      @available(iOS 10.0, *)
      override func userNotificationCenter(_ center: UNUserNotificationCenter, didReceive response: UNNotificationResponse, withCompletionHandler completionHandler:@escaping() -> Void) {
        QGSdk.getSharedInstance().userNotificationCenter(center, didReceive: response)
        super.userNotificationCenter(center, didReceive: response, withCompletionHandler: completionHandler)
      }
    
      @available(iOS 10.0, *)
      override func userNotificationCenter(_ center: UNUserNotificationCenter, willPresent notification: UNNotification, withCompletionHandler completionHandler: @escaping (UNNotificationPresentationOptions) -> Void) {
        QGSdk.getSharedInstance().userNotificationCenter(center, willPresent: notification)
        super.userNotificationCenter(center, willPresent: notification, withCompletionHandler: completionHandler)
      }
    }

### 

6\. Enable rich push notifications

Follow the steps listed in [Configuring Rich Push Notifications](doc:rich-push-notifications-for-flutter) to enable the feature.

### 

7\. Send a test push campaign

[Send a test push campaign](doc:test-notification-for-ios) to verify that your push notification implementation is correct.

# Flutter SDK Web View Support

## 

Overview

The Appier plugin supports web views in Flutter apps via web-to-mobile SDK bridging with the [`InAppWebView`](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_inappwebview)plugin.

Appier Flutter SDK version| Compatible `InAppWebView` plugins versions  
---|---  
2.8.0 and earlier| 5.0.5 to 5.8.0  
3.0.0 or later| 6.0.0  
  
SDK bridging establishes a link between the embedded `InAppWebView` and your native app so that data logged by your website (Appier Web SDK) is automatically passed to the Appier plugin (Appier Flutter SDK). No modifications to your website's logging implementation are required.

### 

Migrating from Flutter SDK 2.8.0 and earlier

The Appier Flutter SDK 3.0.0 uses version 6.0.0 of the `InAppWebView` plugin, which introduced a breaking change. If you're upgrading to the latest SDK version from Appier Flutter SDK 2.8.0 or earlier, please follow the steps in the [`InAppWebView` migration guide](https://inappwebview.dev/docs/migration-guide/) to ensure your web views continue to function properly.

* * *

## 

Initializing an SDK bridge in the `InAppWebView` widget

Initialize a web-to-mobile SDK bridge in an `InAppWebView` widget by hooking into the `onWebViewCreated` and `onLoadStart` events. Enable the bridge using `AppierFlutter.enableWebSdkBridge()`.

Dart
    
    
    InAppWebView(
      ...
      onWebViewCreated: (controller) async {
        ...
        await AppierFlutter.enableWebSdkBridge(
            inAppWebViewController: controller);
        ...
      },
      onLoadStart: (controller, url) async {
        ...
        await AppierFlutter.enableWebSdkBridge(
            inAppWebViewController: controller);
        ...
      });
      ...
    },

* * *

## 

SDK bridge verification

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Prerequisites
> 
> [Integrate the Appier Web SDK with your website](doc:integrating-with-the-aiqua-web-sdk) and verify the integration in a desktop browser before configuring a web SDK bridge.

Complete the following steps to verify that the SDK bridge is working.

  1. Load your website with the `InAppWebView` (generally via `initialUrlRequest`).
  2. Ensure `AppierFlutter.enableWebSdkBridge()` is hooked into `onWebViewCreated` and `onLoadStart`.
  3. Run your app and open the `InAppWebView` screen—this step initializes the Appier Web SDK.
  4. The Appier Web SDK will then initiate a handshake with the Appier plugin. If the SDK bridge has been configured properly, you'll see a message like this in your Flutter app's debug console:



Shell
    
    
    flutter: {message: [WebSdkBridge] Posting message: {"name":"request","body":{"id":"...","name":"getVersion","body":null}}, messageLevel: 0}

  6. Interact with your website so that events and attributes are logged by the Web SDK.
  7. Check the AIQUA Dashboard as described in [these checkpoint steps](doc:event-and-profile-logging-for-flutter#checkpoint) to verify that data logged from your `InAppWebView` screen is captured by the Flutter SDK.

# Getting Started with AIQUA

Using AIQUA, you can engage your customers across various channels from a single platform. In a nutshell, AIQUA allows you to:

  * **[Collect user data](doc:user-data-collection)** including user behaviors on your websites and apps as well as your own set of user data (e.g. your CRM system).
  * **[Segment audience](doc:segments-create)** using the data collected as conditions.
  * Create customized **[campaigns](doc:campaigns-getting-started)** to target different audience segments.
  * Access [**Performance reports**](doc:performance-and-reports-campaign-performance-view-performance) to understand how your campaigns are performing.



* * *

## 

What can I know about my users?

Having user data is crucial in creating campaigns that are relevant to your users. By integrating with Appier Enterprise Service SDK ("Appier SDK"), you will be able to collect the following data about your online users.

  * User attributes from your websites and apps (e.g. email submitted through account registration)
  * User events from your websites and apps (e.g. a user added products to cart)



In addition, you may have your own set of data for your registered members (e.g. your CRM system) that you can upload to AIQUA.

  * Offline user attributes (e.g. user's birthday from your CRM system)
  * Offline user events (e.g. purchase data of a registered member in your physical stores)



By linking the above online and offline data, AIQUA helps you gain a holistic view of your users across platforms. See [User Data Collection](doc:user-data-collection) for more details.

* * *

## 

What can I do with AIQUA?

Once you have data about your users, you can segment audience and create personalized campaigns. Here's an example on how you can use AIQUA to reduce cart abandonment.

  * **Collect user data** : Some users logged in to your website and added products to their shopping cart. By having purchase data from your online and offline platforms on AIQUA, you can single out the users who did not proceed to checkout.

  * **Segment audience** : On the AIQUA dashboard, you can create an audience segment to include users who have added products to cart, and then exclude those who have purchased. You now have a segment of users who left products in the cart without checking out.


![](https://files.readme.io/0ee98e3-Screen_Shot_2021-01-08_at_10.23.02_AM.png)

  * **Create customized campaign** : Now you can create an email campaign to remind users about products forgotten in their carts and offer free shipping. By utilizing AIQUA's [Dynamic Content](doc:dynamic-content-for-personalizing-creatives) feature, you can include each user's name and information about the actual products in each user's cart.

![](https://files.readme.io/9c218cd-Screen_Shot_2021-01-08_at_1.10.58_AM.png)   


To be able to collect user data and create campaigns, you will need to complete the following integrations.

* * *

## 

1\. Integrate platforms with the Appier SDK

First, you need to integrate your website and app with the Appier Enterprise Service SDK ("Appier SDK"). This enables your website and app to show campaign notifications to users, and to collect basic user data such as cookies, device types, and site visits.

See instructions on how to integrate different platforms:

  * **Website:** See [Integrating with the Appier Web SDK](doc:integrating-with-the-aiqua-web-sdk).
  * **Android App:** See [Android SDK Overview](doc:android-sdk-overview).
  * **iOS App:** See [iOS SDK Overview](doc:ios-sdk-integration-overview).



> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
>   * If your website is using multiple domains (e.g. [www.abc.com](http://www.abc.com), [www.abc2.com](http://www.abc2.com)) or subdomains (e.g. blog.abc.com, shop.abc.com), refer to [Cross-Domain Integration](doc:cross-domain-integration).
> 
>   * If your mobile app uses React Native framework, refer to: **React Native:** See [Installing the SDK via React Native](doc:installing-the-sdk-via-react-native).
> 
> 


* * *

## 

2\. Collect custom user data

The basic user data the Appier SDK can automatically collect by default is called **default user data**. In addition to default user data, you need to decide what other data you want to collect about your users and set your website and app to collect these **custom user data**.

  * [User data collection](doc:user-data-collection): Read the overview on how user data is tracked and used in AIQUA.
  * [Default user data](doc:default-aiqua-parameters): See the list of default events and attributes collected by the Appier SDK.
  * [Custom user data](doc:custom-user-data): See how to collect custom events and attributes.



* * *

## 

3\. Upload offline user data

If you have additional user data in your database (e.g. your CRM system), you can upload these data to AIQUA using these methods:

  * [Upload via dashboard as a CSV file](doc:segments-upload-user-attributes)
  * [Upload via API](ref:bulk-upload-offline-users)



* * *

## 

4\. Third-party integrations

Set up the marketing channels you'd like to use to send campaigns via email, SMS, LINE, or Kakao.

[ ![Email](https://files.readme.io/ab6dcf2217131f9965e515b696f5229bd5615d8c54e7c7670c342ad9c4c94509-Mail.png) Email ](/docs/campaigns-getting-started-email) [ ![SMS/MMS](https://files.readme.io/10188113e00cd907230e1b68bf23499b6943297c8f6c3714b589a936d253e7b6-SMS.png) SMS/MMS ](/docs/campaigns-getting-started-sms-mms) [ ![LINE](https://files.readme.io/aa8cd57fab5f7b421d8c3b928c3a507cd5fd9aaae3d9b8e739dae61b15a5d681-LINE.png) LINE ](/docs/campaigns-getting-started-line) [ ![Kakao](https://files.readme.io/b33abe057f05b53ec7eb5da1a9879758c5e46e9170ae2f7c027e5e3809400705-KaKao_Talk.png) Kakao Moment ](/docs/campaigns-getting-started-kakao-moment) [ ![Kakao](https://files.readme.io/b33abe057f05b53ec7eb5da1a9879758c5e46e9170ae2f7c027e5e3809400705-KaKao_Talk.png) Kakao (Chingu Talk) ](/docs/campaigns-getting-started-kakao-chingu-talk)

# Handling Push Notifications

To handle the push notifications (both silent and foreground) and push notification events in your app, add the methods described below into your app delegate (`AppDelegate.swift`).

In addition, you can use `isAppierPush:` to handle push notifications sent by Appier in any of the app delegate methods if your app will also receive notifications from other services.

* * *

## 

App delegate methods for handling push notifications

Add the methods provided below in your app delegate to handle:

  * Events for push notifications
  * Silent push notifications
  * Foreground push notifications



### 

1\. Handling events for push notifications

Add `userNotificationCenter:didReceive:withCompletionHandler:` into your app delegate to handle events for push notifications:

`userNotificationCenter:didReceive:withCompletionHandler:` is called whenever the user responds to the notification by opening the application, dismissing the notification, or choosing the `UNNotificationAction`.

  * The delegate must be set before the application returns from `applicationDidFinishLaunching`
  * This method is required for [carousel](doc:creatives-ios-push-carousel) and [slider](doc:creatives-ios-push-slider) to work



SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // Handle click and deep link events for push notification
    @available(iOS 10.0, *)
    func userNotificationCenter(_ center: UNUserNotificationCenter, didReceive response: UNNotificationResponse, withCompletionHandler completionHandler:@escaping() -> Void) {
      QGSdk.getSharedInstance().userNotificationCenter(center, didReceive: response)
      completionHandler()
    }
    
    
    // handling the click and deeplink events from push notification
    - (void)userNotificationCenter:(UNUserNotificationCenter *)center didReceiveNotificationResponse:(UNNotificationResponse *)response withCompletionHandler:(void(^)(void))completionHandler API_AVAILABLE(ios(10.0)){
      [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] userNotificationCenter:center didReceiveNotificationResponse:response];
      completionHandler();
    }

### 

2\. Handling silent push notifications

Add `application:didReceiveRemoteNotification:fetchCompletionHandler:` into your app delegate to handle silent push notifications.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    // Handle silent push notifications
    // pass completion handler UIBackgroundFetchResult accordingly
    func application(_ application: UIApplication, didReceiveRemoteNotification userInfo: [AnyHashable : Any], fetchCompletionHandler completionHandler: @escaping (UIBackgroundFetchResult) -> Void) {
      let QG = QGSdk.getSharedInstance()
      QG.application(application, didReceiveRemoteNotification: userInfo)
      completionHandler(UIBackgroundFetchResult.noData)
    }
    
    
    // used for silent push handling
    // pass completion handler UIBackgroundFetchResult accordingly
    - (void)application:(UIApplication *)application didReceiveRemoteNotification:(nonnull NSDictionary *)userInfo fetchCompletionHandler:(nonnull void(^)(UIBackgroundFetchResult))completionHandler
    {
      [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] application:application didReceiveRemoteNotification:userInfo];
      completionHandler(UIBackgroundFetchResultNoData);
    }

### 

3\. Handling foreground push notifications

Add `userNotificationCenter:willPresentLwithCompletionHandler:` into your app delegate to handle foreground push notifications.

`userNotificationCenter:willPresentLwithCompletionHandler:` is only called if the application is in the foreground. The notification won't be shown if this method is not implemented or the handler is not called in a timely manner. The application can choose to have the notification as a sound, badge, alert, and in the notification list. This must be based on whether the notification's information is otherwise visible to the user.

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    @available(iOS 10.0, *)
    func userNotificationCenter(_ center: UNUserNotificationCenter, willPresent notification: UNNotification, withCompletionHandler completionHandler: @escaping (UNNotificationPresentationOptions) -> Void) {
      QGSdk.getSharedInstance().userNotificationCenter(center, willPresent: notification)
      completionHandler([.alert, .badge, .sound]);
    }
    
    
    - (void)userNotificationCenter:(UNUserNotificationCenter *)center willPresentNotification:(UNNotification *)notification withCompletionHandler:(void(^)(UNNotificationPresentationOptions options))completionHandler API_AVAILABLE(ios(10.0)){
      [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] userNotificationCenter:center willPresentNotification:notification];
      UNNotificationPresentationOptions option = UNNotificationPresentationOptionBadge | UNNotificationPresentationOptionSound | UNNotificationPresentationOptionAlert;
      completionHandler(option);
    }

## 

Handling push notifications from Appier

If your app will also receive push notifications from services other than Appier, use `isAppierPush:` to determine whether a push notification was sent by Appier.

The following code sample demonstrates one way to implement a notification handler that treats notifications differently depending on whether they were sent by Appier or not by using `isAppierPush:`:

SwiftObjective-C
    
    
    @available(iOS 10.0, *)
    func userNotificationCenter(_ center: UNUserNotificationCenter, didReceive response: UNNotificationResponse, withCompletionHandler completionHandler:@escaping() -> Void) {
      let isAppierPush = QGSdk.getSharedInstance().isAppierPush(response.notification.request.content.userInfo)
      if (isAppierPush) {
        // Handle push notifications from Appier
        QGSdk.getSharedInstance().userNotificationCenter(center, didReceive: response)
        completionHandler()
      } else {
        // Handle other push notifications
      }
    }
    
    
    - (void)userNotificationCenter:(UNUserNotificationCenter *)center didReceiveNotificationResponse:(UNNotificationResponse *)response withCompletionHandler:(void(^)(void))completionHandler API_AVAILABLE(ios(10.0)){
      BOOL isAppierPush = [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] isAppierPush:response.notification.request.content.userInfo];
      if (isAppierPush) {
        // Handle push notifications from Appier
        [[QGSdk getSharedInstance] userNotificationCenter:center didReceiveNotificationResponse:response];
        completionHandler();
      } else {
        // Handle other push notifications
      }
    }
